title: Java Tutorial
summary: Java source expresses typed operations that are compiled for a declared platform release and executed by a compatible runtime.
body:
Java source expresses typed operations that are compiled for a declared platform release and executed by a compatible runtime.

Start with one complete program

Read JDK, JVM, and the first program before debugging syntax in a large project. Compile from a terminal once so a missing compiler, an incorrect classpath, and an exception inside the program do not look like the same failure.

Follow the dependencies

Work through values and arrays before object design. Methods pass values; a copied object reference still points to one object. That rule explains later questions about mutable lists and defensive copies.

Keep the operations visible

After the core modules, move to Java Collections for List, Map, and Deque decisions. Advanced Java covers generic bounds, failure handling, file resources, streams, and worker ownership.

Common Mistakes

Do not treat a roadmap as a substitute for running the programs. Predict each output, change one condition, and test the failure cases. These lessons use Java 8-compatible syntax and APIs unless the page states another requirement.

Continue beyond the object model

Use Advanced Java for runtime inspection, database transactions, HTTP request policies, build tools, tests, and version-labelled Java 17/21 features. Practice graph traversal and cached subproblems, then run the stock ledger project.

Working through this section

The curriculum below groups the canonical pages for this section. Open a lesson to see its release label, operation contract and connected topics. Examples can also be linked from another section without creating a second copy of the same page.

Compile the stated program with a compatible JDK and compare its result with the displayed output. Read the rejected-input and ownership clauses before changing the input. Local self-checks and downloaded programs do not imply a server-side code judge or a production service.

Further Java API boundaries

Inspect filesystem changes, database results, and owned subprocesses.

  • Java walkFileTree: visit failures without hiding incomplete scans
  • Java WatchService: register, consume, and reset each key
  • Java WatchService OVERFLOW: reconcile against directory state
  • Java DirectoryStream: close iteration and reject silent truncation
  • Java symbolic links: inspect attributes without claiming race safety
  • Java JDBC batches: inspect update counts and own rollback
  • Java ResultSet: cursor position and SQL NULL are separate states
  • Java JDBC generated keys: validate one insert and one returned identity
  • Java JDBC fetch size: a hint, not a memory guarantee
  • Java ProcessBuilder: pass command tokens without a shell
  • Java Process.waitFor timeout: terminate and reap the owned child
  • Java file, JDBC, and subprocess boundaries quiz

Further Java network and concurrency boundaries

Inspect request targets, response ownership, and parallel work.

  • Java HTTP query values: encode data without changing URI structure
  • Java HttpClient redirects: check the next origin before resending
  • Java HttpClient deadlines: separate connection and request timeouts
  • Java streaming HTTP bodies: close the stream and cap retained bytes
  • Java Retry-After: parse a bounded server delay without inventing a retry
  • Java HttpClient cookies: make session storage an owned policy
  • Java RecursiveTask: split work only above a measured threshold
  • Java ForkJoinPool: own a custom pool and its shutdown
  • Java ManagedBlocker: declare a rare blocking wait to the pool
  • Java fork/join failures: one failed task does not roll back sibling work
  • Java parallel streams: reduce values instead of mutating shared results
  • Java HTTP and fork/join decisions quiz

Further Java channel and runtime topics

Inspect byte progress, file ownership, and JVM measurements.

  • Java FileChannel.write: finish the buffer before reporting success
  • Java positioned FileChannel.read: detect a short record without moving the cursor
  • Java FileChannel.transferTo: verify the byte count on every pass
  • Java FileChannel.force: distinguish written bytes from forced storage
  • Java FileLock: coordinate one byte range with a shared protocol
  • Java FileChannel.truncate: cut only after validating the recovery offset
  • Java AsynchronousFileChannel: own the buffer through completion
  • Java ThreadMXBean deadlocks: diagnose platform-thread cycles
  • Java ThreadMXBean CPU time: check support and the disabled state
  • Java MemoryMXBean: read used, committed, and an optional maximum
  • Java ClassLoadingMXBean: separate live classes from lifetime totals
  • Java file channels and JVM observations quiz

Further Java XML and archive topics

Inspect parsing, compression, and file publication limits.

  • Java DOM parsing: deny external XML access at the factory
  • Java StAX: pull XML events under a count and entity policy
  • Java XPath: compile a fixed selection, not user-supplied code
  • Java XML Schema validation: use a trusted schema without external fetches
  • Java XML Transformer: bound serialized output and external access
  • Java XML namespaces: select by URI and local name
  • Java GZIPInputStream: cap bytes after decompression
  • Java GZIPOutputStream: close before using the compressed bytes
  • Java ZipFile entries: reject duplicate names before selection
  • Java ZIP CRC32: detect corruption without claiming authenticity
  • Java ZipOutputStream: close each entry and the archive before publication
  • Java XML and archive boundaries quiz

Further Java concurrency topics

Study concurrent state, timed handoffs, and per-thread cleanup.

  • Java ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent: create a counter once per key
  • Java ConcurrentSkipListMap: inspect an ordered time window
  • Java CopyOnWriteArrayList: dispatch against a listener snapshot
  • Java AtomicReference: publish one immutable map snapshot
  • Java DelayQueue: release retry work only after its deadline
  • Java Exchanger: swap buffers at a two-party rendezvous
  • Java LinkedTransferQueue: wait until a consumer receives work
  • Java LongAccumulator: track a concurrent high-water mark
  • Java ThreadLocal: restore request context when a pooled thread is reused
  • Java LockSupport: park only inside a checked condition loop
  • Java concurrent state and handoff quiz

Further Java language topics

Study generics, dispatch, records, and metadata at runtime.

  • Java generic wildcards: copy from a producer into a consumer
  • Java type erasure: validate elements with an explicit Class token
  • Java bridge methods: preserve overrides after generic erasure
  • Java interface defaults: resolve a two-parent method conflict
  • Java compact record constructors: normalize before field assignment
  • Java instanceof patterns: keep a narrowed value inside its valid scope
  • Java switch expressions: return one value from every state
  • Java sealed hierarchies: switch over permitted request kinds
  • Java annotation retention: expose metadata without pretending it enforces policy
  • Java repeatable annotations: read every declared routing label
  • Java enum constant bodies: keep each fee rule with its tier
  • Java generics and language contracts quiz

Further Java JDBC topics

Study savepoints, typed parameters, cursor lifetime, and driver diagnostics.

  • Java JDBC savepoints: roll back one optional step inside a transaction
  • Java JDBC setNull: bind a nullable column with its SQL type
  • Java JDBC query timeout: bound a statement without claiming a whole-request deadline
  • Java JDBC ResultSet binary streams: read before advancing the cursor
  • Java JDBC read-only mode: use the hint without treating it as authorization
  • Java SQLWarning: inspect nonfatal database diagnostics before reuse
  • Java DatabaseMetaData: check features before depending on them
  • Java JDBC cursor holdability: choose what commit does to a ResultSet
  • Java SQLException chains: preserve SQLState and linked failures
  • Java JDBC binary parameters: cap bytes before binding a BLOB
  • Java JDBC boundary contracts quiz

Further Java asynchronous topics

Study dependent stages, competing results, cancellation, and bulk executor calls.

  • Java thenCompose: flatten a dependent asynchronous request
  • Java thenCombine: join two independent results without serializing them
  • Java applyToEither: use the first normal result of two stages
  • Java exceptionallyCompose: recover with another asynchronous stage
  • Java CompletableFuture join versus get: preserve failure and interruption contracts
  • Java CompletableFuture cancellation: distinguish result status from worker interruption
  • Java ExecutorService invokeAll: wait for a bounded batch with a deadline
  • Java ExecutorService invokeAny: return one successful result from competing tasks
  • Java asynchronous contracts quiz

Further Java runtime topics

Study reflective calls, plugin discovery, module access, and method handles.

  • Java reflection: separate an invoked method failure from lookup failure
  • Java getMethod: resolve an overload by its exact parameter types
  • Java trySetAccessible: handle a denied deep-reflection request
  • Java dynamic proxies: define Object-method behavior explicitly
  • Java ServiceLoader: treat provider discovery as fallible startup work
  • Java Class.forName: inspect an allowlisted class without initializing it
  • Java modules: distinguish exported APIs from open packages
  • Java MethodHandle.invokeExact: make the call-site type part of the contract
  • Java runtime discovery contracts quiz

Further Java collection topics

Study compact sets, range views, and bounded concurrent admission.

  • Java BitSet: distinguish logical length, capacity, and set-bit count
  • Java BitSet nextSetBit: scan a bounded index range without walking gaps
  • Java EnumSet complementOf: derive a default-deny capability set
  • Java EnumSet: retain element type when a source collection is empty
  • Java NavigableSet subSet: account for a live backed range
  • Java PriorityBlockingQueue: add an admission limit to an unbounded priority queue
  • Java CopyOnWriteArraySet: publish against a stable listener snapshot
  • Java LinkedBlockingDeque: bound urgent and normal work in one queue
  • Java specialized collections quiz

title: AITrove Editorial
summary: AI Trove’s editorial process covers original explanations, runnable examples, stated release requirements and corrections.
body:
AI Trove Editorial prepares programming lessons with original explanations, application examples and explicit input and failure contracts.

How material is prepared

AI-assisted drafting is used in this project. Technical facts are checked against official specifications and API documentation; a copied program with different values is not the writing process. Lessons separate public API guarantees from implementation details and name the Java release required by their examples.

What code checks establish

Java examples with complete programs are checked with the stated compiler target and compared with their displayed output. Some examples require documented external dependencies or project fixtures. Reproducible source files accompany the Java lessons. Compilation and local test results do not prove production safety, performance under load or correctness for every possible input.

Review and corrections

Readers can report an incorrect statement, a failing program or a missing boundary through AI Trove contact details. A correction should identify the lesson, Java release, input and observed result. Content dates should reflect a substantive revision rather than an automatic freshness claim.

Editorial limits

This profile describes a process, not a professional qualification. No individual author credentials, independent review, affiliation or search ranking are claimed. Unfinished preview material is kept separate from content marked ready for indexing.

title: Values and control flow
summary: Represent values with types and use branches and loops to choose the work to run.
body:
A Java control-flow statement selects or repeats work using typed values and boolean conditions.

Variables and branches

A variable has a type and a value. A condition selects which branch executes.

int score = 72;
if (score >= 50) {
    System.out.println("Pass");
} else {
    System.out.println("Try again");
}

Practice

Change the score to 49 and predict the output. Then write a loop that prints the values from 1 through 5.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java arrays and bounds, Java Tutorial.

Make each branch cover a deliberate boundary

A parcel routing rule might accept a count between 1 and 500. Test the value below the range, the first accepted value, the last accepted value and the value above it. Testing only a middle value cannot reveal an accidental greater-than sign where greater-than-or-equal was required.

A condition can also protect a later operation. In a null check followed by a length check, short-circuit evaluation prevents dereferencing a missing reference only when the null guard is evaluated first. Reversing the expressions changes failure behaviour. Keep guards close to the operation they protect.

A numeric expression is evaluated under the operand types. Assigning the result of int multiplication to long does not repair an overflow that already happened during multiplication. Promote an operand before the operation when the result needs a wider range. Numeric promotion covers that distinction.

A loop needs progress and a stopping rule

For an indexed array scan, the valid condition is index less than length. Less-than-or-equal reaches an invalid position. Incrementing the index establishes progress; removing that increment can make a correct-looking condition run forever.

Nested loops multiply work when each outer iteration scans the entire inner range. Two independent scans do not: their costs add. Count the iterations that actually execute rather than labeling every pair of loops quadratic.

Start with an empty input and a one-element input before large fixtures. They make stopping conditions visible. After the branch and loop basics, use console input to separate invalid input from valid values that fail a business rule.

Common Mistakes

Check empty inputs and invalid values before applying this operation to application data. State whether a method edits shared state or returns a separate value.

title: Methods and objects
summary: Split a task into named operations and connect data to behavior.
body:
A Java method defines a named operation with parameter types, a return type, and a body; callers pass argument values into a new invocation.

Define what the operation promises

A calculation should state its input range, units, failure behavior, and whether it changes caller-owned state. A method named totalCents that accepts an array should not silently store that array for unrelated later work.

The batch below uses positive and zero invoice line values, rejects negative values, and accumulates as long. Math.addExact makes long overflow a failure rather than wrapping into a plausible total. This is a local calculation, not a payment operation.

Parameter values are copied into each invocation. Copying an array reference does not copy its contents. The method only reads the array; see pass-by-value and shared references before adding mutation.

Overloading is a compile-time choice

Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter lists. Return type alone cannot distinguish two overloads with the same parameters. The compiler chooses an applicable signature from the declared argument types; runtime instance overriding is a separate dispatch rule.

Varargs allows a variable-length argument list by presenting an array parameter inside the method. It can introduce an array allocation at a call site. Passing an existing compatible array supplies that array reference rather than automatically creating a detached copy.

Working program

public class InvoiceMethodContract {
    static long totalCents(int[] lineAmounts) {
        if (lineAmounts == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Missing amounts");
        long total = 0L;
        for (int amount : lineAmounts) {
            if (amount < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Negative line amount");
            total = Math.addExact(total, amount);
        }
        return total;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(totalCents(new int[] {1250, 0, 750}));
        System.out.println(totalCents(new int[0]));
    }
}

Output

2000
0

Cost and design choices

The operation visits n line amounts in O(n) time and uses O(1) extra local state. The supplied array is not cloned. A new method frame is not equivalent to a new copy of every referenced object.

A small method can still be expensive if it performs remote work or repeatedly traverses a collection. Method length is not a performance measure. Keep side effects visible in the contract and test empty, invalid, and boundary inputs.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not overload only by return type.
  • Do not describe a passed reference as a copied object.
  • Do not silently return zero for invalid input when zero is also a valid result.
  • Do not ignore integer range when choosing an accumulator.

Connect the contracts

Compare the boundary explained in Java Collections with the assumptions made by this program.

title: Java exceptions: recovery boundaries and failure context
summary: An exception transfers control from a failing operation to a matching handler while unwinding calls that do not handle it.
body:
An exception transfers control from a failing operation to a matching handler while unwinding calls that do not handle it.

Catch what the boundary can handle

A parsing boundary can reject malformed input. It usually cannot repair an unrelated programming error such as an invalid internal array index. Catching Exception around an entire request obscures that difference.

Checked exceptions participate in compile-time handling or declaration requirements. RuntimeException subclasses are unchecked. Neither category proves that a failure is recoverable; recovery depends on what the current layer can actually do.

The parser translates a NumberFormatException into an IllegalArgumentException with the rejected field context and retains the original cause. That preserves useful diagnostic information without exposing the low-level parser as the public contract.

Do not turn a failure into a plausible value

Returning zero after an invalid quantity can make a bad order look like a valid empty order. Reject it explicitly, or return a structured validation result when callers need to report several field errors together.

The program catches the expected input rejection at a small command boundary and prints a user-facing message. The message names the field but avoids logging the raw input. Sensitive request values should not be copied into every exception and log line.

Exceptions from cleanup also matter. Try-with-resources keeps the primary failure and records relevant close failures as suppressed exceptions. A plain finally block can accidentally replace the original failure with its own.

Working program

public class QuantityValidation {
    static int parseQuantity(String rawQuantity) {
        final int quantity;
        try {
            quantity = Integer.parseInt(rawQuantity);
        } catch (NumberFormatException invalidNumber) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Quantity must be a whole number", invalidNumber);
        }
        if (quantity < 1 || quantity > 500) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Quantity must be between 1 and 500");
        }
        return quantity;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(parseQuantity("12"));
        try {
            parseQuantity("many");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException rejectedInput) {
            System.out.println(rejectedInput.getMessage());
            System.out.println(rejectedInput.getCause().getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
    }
}

Output

12
Quantity must be a whole number
NumberFormatException

Cost and design choices

Parsing work depends on input length. Throwing an exception generally constructs diagnostic state and unwinds the stack; it is a poor default mechanism for a high-volume branch that is expected to fail routinely.

A bounded parser should reject enormous input before attempting expensive processing. An int parser still has a numeric range limit even if the business rule’s maximum is smaller.

Retries belong to a boundary that understands whether repeating the operation is safe. An exception alone does not prove idempotency, nor does it tell a caller whether a remote side effect already occurred.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not swallow an exception and continue with a success-shaped value.
  • Do not lose the original cause when translating a failure.
  • Do not catch Throwable as routine input handling.
  • Do not retry an external operation without considering repeated side effects.

Connect the contracts

Compare the boundary explained in Failures in tasks with the assumptions made by this program.

title: Java generics: invariance, bounds, and type erasure
summary: Generics let declarations express relationships between types so the compiler can reject incompatible values before execution.
body:
Generics let declarations express relationships between types so the compiler can reject incompatible values before execution.

Parameterise the contract

A List<Invoice> states what the list accepts and what its reads return. A raw List discards that relationship and moves errors toward runtime casts. Generic type checking does not validate business rules such as invoice currency or an allowed amount range.

List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>. If it were, a caller receiving the supposed Number list could insert a Double into an Integer list. This is invariance, and it protects writes.

Arrays behave differently: reference arrays are covariant and perform runtime store checks. Do not apply the array assignment rule to a generic list. It describes a different safety model.

Use a bound for the direction of data

A source declared as List<? extends Number> can provide Number values, but you cannot safely add an arbitrary Number to it. Its actual element type might be Integer. A destination declared as List<? super Integer> can accept Integer values, while a read can only promise Object.

The program transfers integers into a Number destination. The upper-bounded source supplies compatible input and the lower-bounded destination accepts the copied integers. This keeps callers flexible without resorting to raw types.

Most generic information is erased from ordinary runtime object types. You cannot use new T(), create a normal new List<String>[] array, or distinguish List<String> from List<Integer> with an instanceof test.

Working program

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

public class TypedBatchTransfer {
    static void transfer(List<? extends Integer> source, List<? super Integer> destination) {
        for (Integer shipmentCount : source) {
            destination.add(shipmentCount);
        }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Integer> dailyCounts = Arrays.asList(4, 7, 2);
        List<Number> report = new ArrayList<>();
        transfer(dailyCounts, report);
        System.out.println(report);
    }
}

Output

[4, 7, 2]

Cost and design choices

The transfer visits n source elements and appends n references. With an ArrayList destination, total append work is amortized O(n), and the destination needs O(n) additional reference storage. Generic bounds do not eliminate allocation or boxing.

List<Integer> stores references to boxed values, not an int array. For large numeric workloads, a primitive array or primitive stream can avoid some wrapper overhead.

Erasure does not make generic declarations useless: it places their main safety checks at compilation. Keep collection contracts typed all the way to the boundary, and validate untrusted runtime data separately.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not use raw types to silence a type mismatch.
  • Do not assume a wildcard source accepts writes of its upper bound.
  • Do not cast a list to a different element type and call that conversion.

Connect the contracts

Compare the boundary explained in Generic function types with the assumptions made by this program.

Apply this contract in Spring

title: Advanced Java
summary: Advanced Java work combines type boundaries, resource ownership, concurrency, runtime inspection and external I/O contracts.
body:
Advanced Java work combines type boundaries, resource ownership, concurrency, runtime inspection and external I/O contracts.

Types before casts

Start with generics and wildcard bounds, then make failure handling explicit. Use Optional for defined absence, not as a way to hide an I/O error.

Execution and ownership

A stream pipeline is not a collection copy, and a lambda is not automatically asynchronous. Keep file handles and worker lifetimes scoped to an owner that can close them.

Common Mistakes

Do not add concurrency before measuring the workload and choosing an admission policy. Do not describe an unbounded queue as safe because the worker count is fixed.

title: Java interview discussion prompts
summary: Practice reasoning rather than memorising one-line answers.
body:
A Java interview answer should separate language contracts, library guarantees and implementation-dependent behaviour before predicting an output.

Questions to explain

1. How is a primitive value different from an object reference? 2. What is the difference between an instance method and a static method? 3. When would you choose a list rather than a set?

A useful answer structure

Define the concept, give a tiny example and explain one tradeoff. Ask a follow-up question if the problem lacks context.

Try it

Write a two-minute explanation of why a mutable object can be changed through a reference even when the reference variable is final.

Trace a contract, then state the caveat

For an equality question, ask whether the operator compares primitive values, object identity or an equals implementation. String interning can make an incorrect identity test appear to work for literals. A runtime-created value exposes the difference. Follow up by describing stable hash keys rather than reciting only an equals slogan.

For a pass-by-value question, separate the copied reference from the shared object. A method can mutate the object reachable through the copied reference; assigning its parameter to another object does not replace the caller’s variable. The runnable reference example makes both effects observable.

For a collection complexity question, name the operation and its precondition. LinkedList insertion after an already positioned iterator differs from insertion at an index that first requires traversal. An answer that says all insertions are constant-time hides the lookup cost.

Turn a prediction into a checked example

Write the smallest complete program that preserves the disputed condition, compile it for the stated Java release and compare the output. For concurrency, one observed output is not proof that no other interleaving exists. Explain the visibility or synchronization rule that constrains possible outcomes.

A strong answer also distinguishes a guarantee from a diagnostic. ConcurrentModificationException is not a lock, and a garbage collector is not a deterministic resource closer. Use resource scopes to close files and connections.

Continue with object-contract questions and concurrency reasoning. Predict a failure case as well as the ordinary result, then explain which change repairs the violated contract.

Common Mistakes

Check empty inputs and invalid values before applying this operation to application data. State whether a method edits shared state or returns a separate value.

title: Sum an integer array
summary: Use a loop and an accumulator, including the empty-array case.
body:
An array sum folds each element into an accumulator; the chosen numeric range and empty-input result are part of its contract.

Task

Return the sum of an integer array. Assume the sum fits in an int.

Example solution

static int sum(int[] values) {
    int total = 0;
    for (int value : values) {
        total += value;
    }
    return total;
}

Check your work

{1, 2, 3} returns 6. An empty array returns 0. Decide separately how your program should handle a null input; this version assumes a non-null array.

Define the range before optimizing

The existing method assumes the sum fits in int. That is a precondition, not a check implemented by ordinary addition. A pair of large positive values can wrap to a negative result. Decide whether the application should reject overflow with Math.addExact or accumulate into a wider long result.

An empty array returns zero because zero is the additive identity. Null is not an empty array. Treating the two as equivalent can hide missing data, so either reject null explicitly or document an intentional default at the caller’s boundary.

Negative elements are valid under this arithmetic contract. A method that silently skips them is no longer a sum. Test positive-only, negative-only, mixed-sign and zero-filled arrays before reusing the calculation for a ledger.

Compare against an independent expectation

A test should compare the returned result with a known total and fail when the values differ. Printing a total and visually accepting it is too easy to miss in a larger test run. Include a case that reaches the chosen maximum boundary and a case that exceeds it under a rejecting policy.

The loop visits each element once, so it performs O(n) work and uses O(1) extra storage. Sorting before summing adds work without changing the arithmetic result under exact integer addition. Converting the array to a list adds allocation unless another part of the application actually needs that representation.

A parallel sum needs a defined combination rule and adds task overhead. For floating-point values, regrouping additions can change rounding results; that is a different numeric contract. See decimal calculations when exact business rounding is required.

Common Mistakes

Check empty inputs and invalid values before applying this operation to application data. State whether a method edits shared state or returns a separate value.

title: Your first Java program
summary: Connect the entry point to a visible result.
body:
A conventional Java command-line entry point is a public static main method that the launcher calls with a String array of command-line arguments.

Program

public class Hello {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, AITrove!");
    }
}

Output

Hello, AITrove!

Practice

Save as Hello.java. With a JDK installed, compile with javac Hello.java and run with java Hello. Change the message and repeat.

Keep the source name and launched name separate

The source filename matches the public class name in this example: Hello.java contains public class Hello. javac creates Hello.class. The ordinary class launcher receives Hello without a .java or .class suffix; it searches the classpath for compiled code.

A package declaration changes the launched name. A class in a package is launched by its qualified name, and the classpath must point at the root containing that package directory. Running from the wrong directory can therefore fail even when compilation succeeded.

Compilation and execution are separate failure boundaries. A missing javac executable is a toolchain problem. A compiler error is a source/type problem. A class-not-found error is a launch/classpath problem. An exception after main starts is an execution problem. Do not edit the print statement to fix all four.

Change one observable condition

Pass a command-line argument and inspect args.length before reading args[0]. Launching with no arguments supplies an empty array, so an unchecked first-element access fails. That small change introduces an actual input contract without requiring console parsing.

System.out prints text to a stream. It does not return the printed value from main or persist a business record. A test that needs to examine computed results is easier to write when calculation is in a method and printing is kept at the boundary.

Use the JDK setup lesson for compile/run commands and package layout for multi-file applications. This entry-point program performs constant work and allocates only its small output-related state.

title: Java reading-list project: validated titles and explicit file persistence
summary: A persisted reading list separates validated in-memory membership from the file snapshot that survives a process restart.
body:
A persisted reading list separates validated in-memory membership from the file snapshot that survives a process restart.

Java 8+. This is a complete program using JDK classes.

Define the file format and save boundary

This project stores one nonempty UTF-8 title per line. Titles cannot contain line breaks, and the list is capped at ten thousand entries. The format deliberately has no quoted multiline field grammar. Changing that requirement needs a new parser and compatibility decision.

Adding or removing a title changes only the live list. save creates a staged file and then replaces the named snapshot. Loading parses private list state before returning the restored object, so an invalid file does not expose a half-restored list to callers.

An ordinary move does not claim a crash-durable transaction. A production store needs a tested replacement policy, filesystem capability checks, durability requirements and concurrent-writer coordination. This program is a local single-writer project with no synchronization between processes.

Run the acceptance scenario

The fixture saves two titles, loads a new object, removes one title from the new object and loads the file again. The last count stays two because removal alone is not a save. The temporary directory is cleaned up after the scenario. To retain data in a real CLI, give the application an explicitly owned persistent path instead.

Working program

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.util.*;
public class ReadingListPersistence {
    final List<String> titles=new ArrayList<>();
    void add(String title){
        if(title==null||title.trim().isEmpty()||title.indexOf('\n')>=0||title.indexOf('\r')>=0)throw new IllegalArgumentException("Single nonempty title required");
        if(titles.size()==10000)throw new IllegalArgumentException("Title budget exhausted");
        titles.add(title.trim());
    }
    List<String> snapshot(){return Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(titles));}
    void remove(int index){titles.remove(index);}
    void save(Path destination) throws Exception {
        Path absolute=destination.toAbsolutePath();Path staged=Files.createTempFile(absolute.getParent(),"reading-stage-",".txt");
        try{
            byte[] snapshot=String.join("\n",titles).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            if(snapshot.length>2_000_000)throw new IllegalArgumentException("Snapshot budget exhausted");
            Files.write(staged,snapshot);
            Files.move(staged,absolute,StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        }finally{Files.deleteIfExists(staged);}
    }
    static ReadingListPersistence load(Path source) throws Exception {
        if(Files.size(source)>2_000_000)throw new IllegalArgumentException("File budget exhausted");
        ReadingListPersistence restored=new ReadingListPersistence();
        for(String title:Files.readAllLines(source,StandardCharsets.UTF_8))restored.add(title);
        return restored;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Path directory=Files.createTempDirectory("aitrove-reading-");Path file=directory.resolve("titles.txt");
        try{
            ReadingListPersistence original=new ReadingListPersistence();
            original.add("Concurrency notes");original.add("Collections handbook");original.save(file);
            ReadingListPersistence restored=load(file);System.out.println(restored.snapshot());
            restored.remove(0);System.out.println(restored.snapshot());System.out.println("saved="+load(file).snapshot().size());
        }finally{Files.deleteIfExists(file);Files.deleteIfExists(directory);}
    }
}

Output

[Concurrency notes, Collections handbook]
[Collections handbook]
saved=2

Costs and boundaries

Loading visits O(b) input bytes and stores O(n) titles. The size check is suitable for this owned, unchanged fixture; an adversarial concurrently growing file needs a streaming byte limit during reading. Saving writes O(b) content and needs staged-file storage. Concurrent updates and crash recovery remain outside this project’s contract.

Common Mistakes

  • Removing a title does not implicitly persist it.
  • A pre-read file size check is not a streaming limit under concurrent modification.
  • The staged replacement is not advertised as crash durability.

File operations, Private batch state.

title: Java syntax quick reference
summary: A short reference for values, decisions and repetition.
body:
Java syntax expresses typed declarations, control flow and member access; a reference is useful only when its short forms retain the surrounding validity rules.

Common patterns

Use the reference

Apply these patterns in the array-sum exercise. The table is a starting point, not a complete language reference.

Declarations do not remove ownership rules

A primitive local stores a value, while a reference local identifies an object or holds null. final prevents reassignment of that local or field after its allowed initialization; it does not recursively freeze the referenced object. final List declarations can still permit membership edits.

A method signature states parameter types and a return type. Overloads share a name with different parameter lists, while an override supplies another implementation of an inherited instance method. Return type alone does not create an overload. See compile-time selection when a short signature list leaves ambiguity.

An interface declaration specifies a type contract. Choosing it for a variable allows different implementations, but their operation costs can still differ. List.get on ArrayList and LinkedList shares a signature without sharing the same indexed-access cost.

Keep failure-sensitive forms nearby

An array index must be at least zero and smaller than length. A loop using less-than-or-equal reaches a forbidden final position. An enhanced-for loop avoids explicit indexing but does not permit arbitrary structural modification of its backing collection.

try-with-resources closes owned AutoCloseable values on scope exit. A catch clause handles specified failures; it should not silently convert all failures into an ordinary success result. A finally block is appropriate for releasing an acquired lock, as the lock example shows.

Version matters. Records require a newer source level than Java 8, and the pattern switch lessons in this curriculum declare Java 21. Do not paste their syntax into a Java 8 build and diagnose the parser error as a missing import. Check the page’s release label before compiling.

Common Mistakes

Check empty inputs and invalid values before applying this operation to application data. State whether a method edits shared state or returns a separate value.

title: Linear search in Java
summary: Scan an array and return the position of a target.
body:
Linear search examines elements in sequence until a match is found or the complete search range has been exhausted.

Implementation

static int find(int[] values, int target) {
    for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
        if (values[i] == target) return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

Reasoning

In the worst case every element is checked, so time grows linearly with array length. Extra space stays constant. This version assumes a non-null array.

Check

Try a target at the first position, at the last position and a missing target.

Specify which match is returned

The existing method returns the first matching index. Repeated values do not change that rule. A last-match search must continue after finding an earlier occurrence, while a count-of-matches API must retain a counter rather than return an index.

Minus one represents absence because valid array indexes are non-negative. Returning zero for absence would collide with a real match in the first position. An API returning an object instead needs an explicit missing-value representation, such as Optional, rather than borrowing an unrelated numeric sentinel.

An empty array has no match and executes no loop iterations. A null array is outside this implementation’s input contract and fails before a scan can begin. Put validation at the boundary if callers need a named exception for missing input.

Use the simple scan as a reference

For small test fixtures, a linear scan is a useful reference against which to check a more elaborate index. Compare the actual membership and first-position semantics. A faster method that returns a different duplicate occurrence is not interchangeable when the caller requires the first one.

The best case inspects one element, while absence or a match at the final position requires n comparisons. Extra working storage is O(1). For repeated searches, building a hash index may reduce lookup work but adds storage and changes update costs.

Binary search requires sorted input and has separate duplicate-position choices. Sorting a batch only to answer one lookup may cost more than this scan; include that preprocessing rather than comparing the scan with only the binary-search loop.

Common Mistakes

Check empty inputs and invalid values before applying this operation to application data. State whether a method edits shared state or returns a separate value.

title: List, set or map?
summary: Compare ordered elements, unique values and key-value lookup.
body:
A collection contract describes the operations a caller needs; its implementation determines ordering and performance.

Select by behavior

  • List: an ordered sequence that can contain duplicates.
  • Set: membership with no duplicate elements under the implementation’s equality rules.
  • Map: values associated with keys.
  • Deque: insertions and removals at both ends.

Use ArrayList as a starting point for indexed sequence access. Consider ArrayDeque for endpoint work without null elements. Study LinkedList when cursor edits and the combined List/Deque contract matter.

A contract is narrower than an implementation

Declare List when callers need list operations, but choose the implementation from the actual workload. A contract-compatible substitution can still change performance: repeated indexed access that is cheap on an array-backed list is expensive on linked storage.

Map is not a Collection subtype. Its key set, value collection, and entry set expose views of the mappings with their own mutation rules. Decide whether the caller receives a live view or a copied snapshot.

Common Mistakes

Do not assume a Set preserves insertion order or a Map sorts keys. Those properties depend on the chosen implementation.

Choose an operation and a lifetime

Write the access pattern before naming a collection: endpoint queue, keyed membership, sorted nearest-key lookup or indexed editing. A container that performs one of those well can perform another poorly. Indexed traversal of a linked list can revisit the same chain for every position.

Then define lifetime and ownership. A copied membership snapshot differs from a backed view; both can still share mutable values. An immutable factory can reject nulls that an older caller previously stored, so migration needs data validation rather than a class-name swap.

Finally define concurrency and admission. A concurrent map does not bound distinct keys, and a fixed thread pool does not bound pending tasks. A service queue may need capacity, rejection, interruption and shutdown policies in addition to a FIFO order. None of these Java containers promises durable delivery after process loss.

title: Java Collections
summary: Java collections supply membership, ordering and traversal contracts whose ownership, costs and concurrency behavior differ by implementation.
body:
Java collections supply membership, ordering and traversal contracts whose ownership, costs and concurrency behavior differ by implementation.

Choose the question first

Use a List for ordered values, a Set for membership, a Map for a key-to-value association, or a Deque for endpoint work. Map is part of the collections framework but is not a subtype of Collection.

Ordering is a contract

TreeMap orders keys. LinkedHashMap keeps encounter order. PriorityQueue orders removals but does not supply sorted iteration. Those guarantees answer different questions.

Common Mistakes

Do not choose LinkedList simply because the workload inserts elements: finding an insertion position can dominate the edit. Count traversal, copying, allocation, and synchronisation needs before selecting an implementation.

title: Java basics quiz
summary: Check primitive types, integer division, array bounds and loop behavior with explained Java basics questions.
body:
A Java basics self-check tests value types, expression results, array bounds and loop termination.

Review the contracts

Review primitive types, numeric promotion, conditions and loops before answering.

Choose and explain an answer

Predict the result before choosing an option. Track the declared type and valid index range; the intended business result cannot change the expression's rules.

Select an answer for every question, then check the result and read each explanation. Progress remains in this browser; this is a self-check, not a judged program submission or a credential.

Do not treat integer division as decimal division or use length as the last valid array index.
subject: java-quizzes

questions.prompt: Which type represents true or false?
questions.explanation: boolean has the values true and false.

questions.prompt: What does the array-sum exercise return for an empty array?
questions.explanation: The loop has no elements to visit, so the accumulator remains 0.

questions.prompt: What does int division 7 / 2 return?
questions.explanation: Integer division discards the fractional part toward zero.

questions.prompt: Which array position is the last valid one for length n > 0?
questions.explanation: The array positions form the half-open range from zero up to length.

questions.prompt: What does final StringBuilder prohibit?
questions.explanation: final concerns reference assignment, not the mutability of the referred object.

questions.prompt: What happens when an Integer containing null is used as an int?
questions.explanation: Unboxing cannot obtain a primitive value from a null reference.

questions.prompt: Which compares two String values?
questions.explanation: Value comparison must not depend on accidental interning.

questions.prompt: What does a for-each assignment to an int loop variable change?
questions.explanation: The iteration variable receives a value; assigning it does not assign the array member.

questions.prompt: What does a failed numeric range check need to preserve?
questions.explanation: A rejection-without-mutation contract needs validation before applying state changes.

questions.prompt: What does a short-circuit && skip when its left side is false?
questions.explanation: The right operand is not evaluated when the left false value already determines the result.

questions.prompt: Does casting an already-overflowed int result to long repair it?
questions.explanation: The int operation happened before the widening conversion.

questions.prompt: Can rows of a Java int[][] have different lengths?
questions.explanation: The outer array stores references to row arrays, not one guaranteed rectangular block.

title: JDK, JVM and your first program
summary: A Java toolchain compiles source with javac and runs bytecode with a compatible Java runtime.
body:
A Java toolchain compiles source with javac and runs bytecode with a compatible Java runtime.

Working model

Use a supported JDK that matches your project. Check java -version and javac -version in the same terminal. Different versions usually mean PATH points at two installations. Keep the public class name and source filename identical.

Code

public class OrderReceipt {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Order received: ORD-1042");
    }
}

Save as OrderReceipt.java. Compile with javac OrderReceipt.java, then run java OrderReceipt. The output is Order received: ORD-1042. Run from the directory containing the compiled class, or supply a classpath.

Cost and design choices

Compilation checks names and types. Execution can still fail because a dependency is missing or an input violates an assumption. Start with this small program before adding an IDE or a build tool.

Separate three failure stages

A compiler error means no valid class file was produced for that compilation. A class-not-found error means the launcher could not locate the requested compiled entry point. A stack trace from main means execution started and the program failed later. Keep the command and working directory in the bug report.

The source filename must match a public top-level class name. Java class names are case-sensitive, so a filename accepted on one filesystem can still hide a portability problem. Run the compiled name without a .class suffix.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java variables and primitive types, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Running java OrderReceipt.class is incorrect: java expects a class name here. A newer compiler can emit bytecode that an older JVM cannot run; use --release when targeting an older supported runtime.

Separate toolchain failures from program failures

Check both java -version and javac -version before investigating a program. A machine can launch one installed runtime while its compiler comes from another installation. Keep the compiler release target separate from the compiler installation; javac --release 8 on a newer JDK checks the stated platform API and language boundary.

Compile into a dedicated output directory, then give that directory to the class path. Launch a packaged class by its full binary name, not by a source-file pathname. A missing class and an exception thrown from main occur at different stages; preserving the actual error makes that distinction visible.

The small program verifies compilation and launch. It does not validate an IDE’s test configuration, a dependency resolver or deployment packaging. Once the command-line build works, reproduce the same source roots, release target and runtime selection in the IDE.

title: Java variables and primitive types
summary: A Java variable has a declared type that determines its permitted values and operations.
body:
A Java variable has a declared type that determines its permitted values and operations.

Working model

Use integer types for counts. For this receipt, money is stored as an integer number of paise; the sample excludes currencies whose smallest unit differs. Floating-point values are unsuitable for exact decimal accounting.

Code

long unitPricePaise = 129900L;
int quantity = 3;
long invoiceTotalPaise = Math.multiplyExact(unitPricePaise, quantity);
boolean eligibleForDispatch = quantity > 0;
System.out.println(invoiceTotalPaise);
System.out.println(eligibleForDispatch);

The output is 389700, followed by true. Math.multiplyExact reports overflow rather than silently wrapping. A long has a wider range than an int, but neither grows without a limit.

Cost and design choices

Primitive assignment copies a value. Reference assignment copies a reference; two variables can then identify the same mutable object. That distinction matters when a method changes a list it receives.

Range and initialization boundaries

int arithmetic can wrap without throwing. Widening the destination variable after an overflowing int calculation does not recover the lost value. Convert an operand before the calculation or use checked arithmetic when overflow should reject the operation.

Fields and array elements receive default values; local variables need a definite assignment before use. A default zero may also be a valid business value, so explicitly track absence instead of assuming an unassigned field will be obvious.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java operators and numeric promotion, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Local variables require initialization before use. Integer overflow is not automatically an exception for ordinary arithmetic. For financial systems, validate units, currency, and rounding rules explicitly.

Choose the representation for the allowed values

A quantity that can never be fractional should not become double merely because a parser accepted a decimal token. Integral ranges, overflow behavior and nullability belong to the field contract. A primitive has no null sentinel; an Integer may be absent and can fail during unboxing.

Local variables need a definitely assigned value before reading. Fields have initialization defaults, but a default zero is not evidence that a business value was supplied. Model missing input explicitly at the parsing boundary rather than allowing field defaults to stand in for validation.

Assignments to reference variables copy references. They do not duplicate a list, an array or its nested members. Declare which component owns mutation and test changes through a second alias before describing a value as a snapshot. final prevents reassignment of that variable; it does not freeze a referenced array.

title: Java operators and numeric promotion
summary: Java operators compute values, compare operands, and combine boolean conditions.
body:
Java operators compute values, compare operands, and combine boolean conditions.

Working model

Integer division discards the fractional part. Cast an operand before division when the fraction matters; casting the result afterward cannot recover what was already discarded.

Code

int completedJobs = 7;
int submittedJobs = 10;
double completionRate = (double) completedJobs / submittedJobs;
boolean shouldRetry = submittedJobs > 0 && completionRate < 0.9;
System.out.println(completionRate);
System.out.println(shouldRetry);

The output is 0.7 and true. The cast changes the division to floating-point arithmetic. In a general method, check submittedJobs before computing the rate.

Cost and design choices

The && and || operators short-circuit. A guard on the left can prevent an unsafe expression on the right from executing. A single & on boolean operands evaluates both sides.

Promotion before assignment

For byte and short arithmetic, most ordinary numeric operations promote operands to int. A narrowing assignment needs an explicit conversion or a compound-assignment rule, and narrowing can lose information. The destination type does not select the intermediate expression type.

&& and || short-circuit: the right operand may not execute. Avoid hiding required side effects there. Integer division truncates toward zero; switching the final assigned variable to double does not undo division that already happened as int arithmetic.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java conditions and loops, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Guard against a zero denominator before division. Do not use == to compare string contents. Parentheses are cheap; use them when precedence would force a reader to pause.

Evaluate types before trusting the final value

Two int operands produce int arithmetic unless a conversion changes the operand types first. A long destination does not fix an overflow inside an earlier int addition. Use a widened operand or checked arithmetic when a rejected overflow is the business rule.

Integer division discards the fractional part toward zero. Floating-point division introduces its own rounding and special values; it is not an automatic substitute for decimal money. BigDecimal arithmetic still needs a declared scale and rounding policy at the operation boundary.

Short-circuit boolean operators can skip the right operand. That is useful for a null check followed by a dereference, but it also means a right-hand side effect might never happen. Keep required state changes out of boolean conditions, and parenthesize a compound business rule when precedence could hide its intent.

Related node and runtime checks

Continue with Java checked integer arithmetic: reject overflow before updating state.

More numeric representation boundaries

Continue with Java Math.abs on Integer.MIN_VALUE: detect the one value that cannot turn positive, Java floorDiv and floorMod: assign negative coordinates to stable buckets, Java unsigned int parsing: preserve 32-bit protocol values.

title: Java conditions and loops
summary: Conditions choose a branch; loops repeat work while a condition or iteration source permits it.
body:
Conditions choose a branch; loops repeat work while a condition or iteration source permits it.

Working model

Separate a skip condition from a stop condition. continue skips the remaining work for one iteration; break exits the loop. The difference can leave later records unprocessed.

Code

int[] retryCounts = {0, 1, 4, 2};
int acceptedJobs = 0;
for (int retries : retryCounts) {
    if (retries > 3) {
        continue;
    }
    acceptedJobs++;
}
System.out.println(acceptedJobs);

The output is 3. Each retry count is visited once, so the work is O(n) with O(1) extra space. The enhanced loop fits this case because the code does not need an index.

Cost and design choices

Use a while loop when the number of iterations depends on an external state, but make the state change visible. For bounded retries, a counted loop makes the limit harder to miss.

Loop invariants and exit policies

A loop should make progress toward a condition that can become false. Updating the wrong counter or comparing against an unchanging value can create an infinite loop even when the body appears small.

Use half-open index bounds for arrays: start at zero and stop before length. continue still permits a for loop’s update step, while return exits the method. Do not replace an error with break when the caller needs to know that processing stopped early.

Connected lessons

Continue with Values and control flow, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

A loop ending at index <= array.length accesses one element past the end. Replacing continue with break changes this example to stop at the first rejected record. Unbounded retries can consume resources indefinitely.

State the loop invariant and exit condition

A loop should keep a condition true after every completed iteration: a processed prefix is valid, a remaining counter is non-negative, or the current search interval contains every possible answer. Naming that condition gives the update and exit test something concrete to preserve.

A continue can skip an update when the update lives in the body. A rejected input can therefore repeat forever if the loop retries without consuming it. A break exits only its defined loop or switch scope, so nested search code needs an explicit result boundary rather than assuming every break leaves the method.

Test the zero-iteration case and the final legal iteration. For an array, the final valid position is length minus one. For a half-open search range, the upper boundary is excluded. Switching between these conventions halfway through a method is a common source of missed values or out-of-bounds access.

title: Java arrays and bounds
summary: An array is a fixed-length, indexed container whose elements share a component type.
body:
An array is a fixed-length, indexed container whose elements share a component type.

Working model

Allocate the array when its length is known. Indexing is O(1), but valid indices stop at length - 1. An array with length zero is valid and has no readable element.

Code

int[] dailyOrders = {12, 0, 8, 15};
int totalOrders = 0;
for (int orders : dailyOrders) {
    totalOrders += orders;
}
System.out.println(totalOrders);

The output is 35. Summation visits every element: O(n) time and O(1) extra space. A larger input may overflow an int total, so select the accumulator type from the expected range.

Cost and design choices

An array reference can be shared. Passing dailyOrders into a method does not create a separate array. Copy it when a caller must keep an unchanged snapshot.

Aliasing, covariance, and copying

Arrays.copyOf creates another array but only copies references for object elements. If an element is mutable, both arrays still reach that element. A two-dimensional Java array is an array of row references, so copying the outer array also shares the original rows.

A reference array can be assigned to a wider reference-array type. Its actual component type still controls writes, so storing an incompatible element throws ArrayStoreException. Generic lists use a different invariance rule that catches many such assignments at compilation.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java strings and content equality, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Do not assume every row of a two-dimensional array has the same length. Validate an index before accessing it. An array of object references initially contains null unless each element is assigned.

Distinguish membership copies from nested copies

An array has fixed membership length and mutable slots. Assigning it to another variable shares those slots. clone makes another outer array, but a nested array or mutable element can still be shared. Decide whether callers need independent rows or merely independent outer membership.

Java multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays. Rows can have different lengths and can be null. A loop using the first row’s length for every row invents a rectangular-shape contract that the representation itself does not guarantee.

Bounds checks protect access at runtime but do not make an off-by-one algorithm correct. Test empty input, one element and the final position. A copied snapshot also adds allocation and O(n) element-reference work; it should appear in the method’s space cost rather than vanish behind the word copy.

Related node and runtime checks

Collection views and copy boundaries

Continue with Arrays.asList in Java: fixed-size list backed by the original array, List.copyOf freezes container membership but not mutable elements.

title: Java strings and content equality
summary: String is an immutable sequence of characters; operations return a result rather than editing the existing object.
body:
String is an immutable sequence of characters; operations return a result rather than editing the existing object.

Working model

Use equals for content comparison. The == operator compares references. A constant on the left of equals handles a nullable candidate without dereferencing it.

Code

String paymentStatus = new String("PAID");
boolean dispatchAllowed = "PAID".equals(paymentStatus);
String receiptLabel = paymentStatus.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT);
System.out.println(dispatchAllowed);
System.out.println(receiptLabel);

The output is true and paid. paymentStatus remains PAID. Locale.ROOT makes this machine-facing transformation independent of a user locale.

Cost and design choices

Repeated concatenation inside a large loop can create many intermediate strings. Use StringBuilder for incremental construction. A StringBuilder is mutable, so do not share one between threads without a coordination policy.

Text length is not always character count

String.length counts UTF-16 code units. Some Unicode characters occupy two code units, and a user-perceived character can combine several code points. Indexing and substring boundaries therefore need a defined text model when the input is not restricted to a simple identifier alphabet.

String is immutable, but repeated concatenation in a loop can create intermediate strings and repeated copying. Use a StringBuilder for a growing report, and limit total output size. A small one-off concatenation is a different workload.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java classes and objects, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Strings are not passwords vaults; an immutable string cannot be wiped in place. Unicode characters can span more than one char. Do not assume length counts user-visible characters.

Define equality, positions and encoding separately

String.equals compares the represented character sequence; == compares whether two references point to the same object. Interning can make some reference comparisons appear to work until input comes from a parser or another allocation. Use the value contract directly.

String positions are UTF-16 code-unit positions. A supplementary code point can occupy two units, and several code points can form one displayed unit. A UI character limit and a protocol byte limit therefore need different measurements. Use an explicit charset when moving text across a byte boundary.

The String object does not change when concatenation returns another String. Repeated accumulation in a loop can create substantial copying and temporary objects; a builder makes the intended mutable assembly phase explicit. That optimization does not decide whether the final value needs normalization or a language-specific comparison rule.

title: Java classes and objects
summary: A class defines state and behavior; an object is one instance of that definition.
body:
A class defines state and behavior; an object is one instance of that definition.

Working model

Keep state private when arbitrary writes would violate an invariant. The public operations below permit a task to change status without exposing the stored boolean as a writable field.

Code

public class DispatchTask {
    private boolean completed;

    public void complete() {
        completed = true;
    }

    public boolean isCompleted() {
        return completed;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        DispatchTask task = new DispatchTask();
        task.complete();
        System.out.println(task.isCompleted());
    }
}

The output is true. Each task has its own completed field. A static field would instead belong to the class and would be shared by all instances.

Cost and design choices

Objects are accessed through references. Assigning task to another variable does not clone its state. Make copying explicit when a separate lifecycle is required.

Reachability and object ownership

A constructor does not automatically deep-copy the values passed into it. Storing a caller’s mutable collection keeps a shared reference. If the object promises a snapshot, copy the relevant structure and state how mutable elements are handled.

Garbage collection reclaims unreachable objects, not objects merely labelled temporary in a method name. Static fields, listeners, and captured callbacks can keep entire object graphs reachable. Releasing a reference also does not promptly close an external file or socket.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java constructors and validated state, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Do not expose mutable fields simply to reduce accessor code. A null reference does not identify an object. Calling an instance method through it fails before the method can inspect its arguments.

Make object state valid at publication

A constructor should establish the invariant that every permitted public operation can rely on. A stock object with a negative available count is already invalid before reserve is called. Reject that input rather than requiring every future operation to repair it.

An object can be referenced by several components. Returning its mutable internal list gives callers another mutation path around the class’s validation. Publish a copied or explicitly read-only view according to the required lifetime; a read-only live view still changes when the owner changes its backing state.

Instance fields belong to a particular object, while static fields belong to the loaded class. Moving state to static can accidentally merge independent accounts or requests. It also adds a shared lifetime and coordination requirement that did not exist when each request owned its own object.

Apply this contract in Spring

Spring ApplicationContext: construct and close an object graph, Spring bean scopes: singleton identity is not thread safety. These lessons keep framework assembly separate from the Java contract.

title: Java constructors and validated state
summary: A constructor initializes a new object and can reject inputs that would leave it unusable.
body:
A constructor initializes a new object and can reject inputs that would leave it unusable.

Working model

Require the identifier at creation. The constructor below validates the supplied value before storing it. This keeps every successfully created ticket usable without a later initialize call.

Code

public class SupportTicket {
    private final String ticketId;

    public SupportTicket(String ticketId) {
        if (ticketId == null || ticketId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("ticketId is required");
        }
        this.ticketId = ticketId;
    }

    public String id() {
        return ticketId;
    }
}

A constructor has the class name and no return type. this.ticketId distinguishes the field from the parameter. final prevents reassignment of this field after construction; it does not make every object referenced by a final field immutable.

Cost and design choices

Validation adds work once per creation. That is often cheaper than requiring every operation to recover from missing state. Keep expensive I/O out of constructors when failures need a separate retry policy.

Keep partially built objects private

Do not publish this to another thread or callback before construction finishes. The observer can see an object whose invariants have not been established. Calling an overridable method from a constructor can also dispatch to subclass code before subclass initialization completes.

Validate related fields together. Two fields can each be individually valid while their combination is invalid, such as an end timestamp before a start timestamp. Constructor success should mean the complete object state is usable.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java encapsulation and object ownership, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Adding a return type turns the declaration into a method. Do not call overridable methods from constructors: subclass state may not yet be initialized. Avoid storing mutable input collections without deciding who owns later edits.

Validate before the object escapes

Constructor chaining should lead to one place that establishes the state contract. Duplicated validation in several overloads can drift until one constructor permits a state another rejects. A factory can name distinct creation policies without making callers guess which positional argument combination applies.

Avoid registering this with an external listener or starting a worker while construction is still in progress. Another component can then observe fields before the invariant is established. Finish creation, then let an explicit owner publish the object or start its resources.

Construction can allocate more than the outer object: copied collections, parsed metadata and acquired resources all contribute cost. If the constructor can fail after acquiring a resource, cleanup needs an explicit scope. A simple immutable value constructor should not quietly own a long-lived connection or executor.

title: Java encapsulation and object ownership
summary: Encapsulation keeps an object’s representation behind operations that preserve its rules.
body:
Encapsulation keeps an object’s representation behind operations that preserve its rules.

Working model

Private fields alone do not protect a mutable collection. If a getter returns the internal list, callers can alter it without using your methods. Return a snapshot when that behavior is unwanted.

Code

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;

public class AuditBatch {
    private final List<String> eventIds = new ArrayList<>();

    public void record(String eventId) {
        if (eventId == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("eventId");
        eventIds.add(eventId);
    }

    public List<String> snapshot() {
        return Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(eventIds));
    }
}

Copying takes O(n) time and O(n) space. The returned list cannot be modified through its own methods, and later additions to eventIds do not appear in the copy.

Cost and design choices

This is a shallow copy. It is enough for immutable String values. If the list contains mutable records, their fields can still be shared and changed unless those values are copied too.

A getter can leak ownership

Returning the internal mutable list gives callers a route around the object’s validation methods. An unmodifiable wrapper blocks writes through that wrapper but still reflects changes made through another reference to the backing list.

Choose a snapshot, read-only live view, or explicitly shared collection according to the contract. The choice affects both memory and what a reader can observe over time. Hiding fields with private does not by itself establish that contract.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java inheritance and method overriding, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

An unmodifiable wrapper around the original list is a view, not a snapshot. This class is not thread-safe; copying while another thread writes requires coordination.

Protect every mutation route

Private fields are only one part of encapsulation. A public setter, returned array, live collection view or callback can still permit callers to bypass the intended invariant. Review the whole public surface and every alias it publishes.

Expose an operation such as reserve(quantity) when the rule spans available and reserved counts. Two unrelated setters make the caller responsible for preserving a relation it cannot update atomically. Validate before changing either field and specify the unchanged state on rejection.

An unmodifiable wrapper prevents updates through that wrapper but can still reflect owner updates and expose mutable elements. Independent snapshots need a copy at the correct layer. If multiple workers share the object, the class also needs one stated synchronization rule for reads and compound writes.

title: Java inheritance and method overriding
summary: Inheritance permits a subclass to extend a class; overriding supplies a different implementation of an inherited instance method.
body:
Inheritance permits a subclass to extend a class; overriding supplies a different implementation of an inherited instance method.

Working model

Use inheritance when the subtype must satisfy the same contract. Extending a class just to reuse a helper couples unrelated behavior and can expose operations the subtype should not support.

Code

public class DeliveryCharge {
    public int chargePaise() {
        return 5000;
    }

    static class PickupCharge extends DeliveryCharge {
        @Override
        public int chargePaise() {
            return 0;
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        DeliveryCharge charge = new PickupCharge();
        System.out.println(charge.chargePaise());
    }
}

The output is 0. The reference type permits the call; the object’s runtime class supplies the overridden implementation. The annotation catches a mismatched signature at compilation.

Cost and design choices

Prefer composition when pricing policies should be replaceable independently of the object hierarchy. A contained policy object makes that dependency explicit.

Substitution has behavioral limits

A subclass inherits more than names: callers already have assumptions about the parent’s accepted inputs, results, and state changes. A child that unexpectedly rejects valid parent inputs or changes units breaks those assumptions even if the code compiles.

Prefer composition when the new type needs to use another object without promising that it can replace that object. Inherited mutable protected fields can make invariants harder to control because several layers can alter them.

Connected lessons

Continue with Java interfaces and replaceable behavior, Java Tutorial.

Common Mistakes

Overloading changes the parameter list and is a different operation from overriding. Static methods do not dispatch like overridden instance methods. A subclass must preserve expectations established by the parent contract.

Preserve the parent contract

An override must keep the behavior callers of the parent type are entitled to use. Narrowing an accepted input range or introducing an unrelated failure can break a caller that never names the subtype. Choose inheritance for substitutable behavior, not merely for reusing a few implementation lines.

Instance-method dispatch uses the actual object type after overload selection has chosen a method signature. Static methods and fields do not follow that same dispatch rule. Inspect the declared receiver and argument types before explaining an overloaded call trace.

A base constructor that invokes an overridable method can call subtype code before subtype initialization is complete. Keep construction-time invariant setup away from that virtual dispatch. Composition often makes resource ownership and independent policy changes easier to represent than a deep inheritance chain.
