title: Java SwingWorker: background work and event-thread publication
summary: SwingWorker runs background work separately from the Swing event dispatch thread and delivers completion callbacks to the event thread.
body:
SwingWorker runs background work separately from the Swing event dispatch thread and delivers completion callbacks to the event thread.

This program targets Java 8 without preview flags. Use a full JDK for compiler-based examples.

The UI thread is an ownership boundary

A desktop receipt viewer should not parse a large import inside a button listener. That listener runs on the event dispatch thread. Blocking it prevents repainting and input handling, so the window can look frozen even when the parser is making progress.

The background task returns a result rather than modifying a Swing label directly. done obtains the completed result and updates the model on the event thread. The fixture uses an atomic reference only to transfer its observed label back to the test thread; the Swing label itself remains event-thread-owned.

Completion and waiting are different operations

Calling get on a still-running worker from the event thread recreates the blocking problem. done is different because the task has already completed; failure still needs handling because get can throw ExecutionException or InterruptedException. Preserve interruption when catching the latter.

This headless program verifies background execution, event-thread completion and the label value without opening a window. It is a Swing threading fixture, not a full desktop application. A real application still needs cancellation, input disabling and an explicit failure display.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference;
import javax.swing.JLabel;
import javax.swing.SwingUtilities;
import javax.swing.SwingWorker;
public class ReceiptViewerWorker {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        AtomicReference<String> observed = new AtomicReference<>();
        CountDownLatch completed = new CountDownLatch(1);
        SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(() -> {
            JLabel label = new JLabel("Waiting");
            SwingWorker<Integer, Void> worker = new SwingWorker<Integer, Void>() {
                protected Integer doInBackground() {
                    if (SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()) throw new IllegalStateException("Work on UI thread");
                    return 6;
                }
                protected void done() {
                    try {
                        if (!SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()) throw new IllegalStateException("Completion off UI thread");
                        label.setText("Imported="+get()); observed.set(label.getText());
                    } catch (InterruptedException failure) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); observed.set("interrupted"); }
                    catch (Exception failure) { observed.set("failed"); }
                    finally { completed.countDown(); }
                }
            };
            worker.execute();
        });
        if (!completed.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) throw new IllegalStateException("Completion deadline");
        System.out.println(observed.get());
    }
}

Output

Imported=6

Costs and boundaries

The fixture does constant background work and retains one label and one worker. Application cost follows the actual parser and its result, not SwingWorker itself. Publishing thousands of small UI updates can overwhelm the event queue; coalesce progress instead of repainting for every row. A timeout in this test bounds its wait, not the latency of every desktop operation.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not mutate Swing components from doInBackground.
  • Do not wait for unfinished work on the event thread.
  • Cancellation needs cooperation from the background operation.

title: Java BufferedImage: deterministic raster output without a window
summary: BufferedImage stores a raster and a color model so Java code can render and inspect image pixels without displaying a desktop window.
body:
BufferedImage stores a raster and a color model so Java code can render and inspect image pixels without displaying a desktop window.

This program targets Java 8 without preview flags. Use a full JDK for compiler-based examples.

Pixel checks are narrower than screenshots

A receipt preview can be generated on a server where no display is available. The program creates a small ARGB image and paints a solid status area. It tests exact pixels in that rectangle rather than relying on a screenshot tool or a font installed on the machine.

Text rendering has extra dependencies: font choice, metrics, antialiasing and platform rasterization can change its pixels. This program deliberately contains no text, so its acceptance check establishes geometry and color only. A production receipt renderer needs a separate layout and text test.

Release the drawing context

Graphics2D holds rendering state and must be disposed after the painting operation. The image stays usable after disposal; disposing the context does not erase its pixels. A try/finally block keeps that lifecycle clear when drawing fails.

The program writes a PNG to memory, decodes it and checks both a painted pixel and an untouched transparent pixel. It rejects a missing encoder or failed decode rather than treating an empty byte array as a successful image. The fixture encodes its own image; it does not parse an unbounded user upload.

Working program

import java.awt.Color;
import java.awt.Graphics2D;
import java.awt.image.BufferedImage;
import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream;
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import javax.imageio.ImageIO;
public class ReceiptStatusRaster {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        BufferedImage image = new BufferedImage(40, 20, BufferedImage.TYPE_INT_ARGB);
        Graphics2D paint = image.createGraphics();
        try { paint.setColor(new Color(20, 70, 100)); paint.fillRect(4, 3, 8, 6); }
        finally { paint.dispose(); }
        ByteArrayOutputStream bytes = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        if (!ImageIO.write(image, "png", bytes)) throw new IllegalStateException("Missing PNG encoder");
        BufferedImage restored = ImageIO.read(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes.toByteArray()));
        if (restored == null) throw new IllegalStateException("PNG decode failed");
        System.out.println(restored.getWidth()+"x"+restored.getHeight());
        System.out.println(restored.getRGB(4, 3) == new Color(20, 70, 100).getRGB());
        System.out.println(restored.getRGB(0, 0) == 0);
    }
}

Output

40x20
true
true

Costs and boundaries

An ARGB raster needs storage proportional to width times height, with additional encoder buffers. Validate dimensions before multiplication and allocation when dimensions come from outside the application. Compressed file size is not a reliable bound on decoded memory. This example owns only an 800-pixel image and does not establish upload safety or typography fidelity.

Common Mistakes

  • Dispose every created Graphics2D context.
  • Do not infer decoded memory size from compressed byte count.
  • Pixel assertions for flat geometry do not verify text layout across platforms.

title: Java annotation processing: reject invalid declarations during compilation
summary: An annotation processor inspects compiler elements during processing rounds and can reject a declaration with a compile-time diagnostic.
body:
An annotation processor inspects compiler elements during processing rounds and can reject a declaration with a compile-time diagnostic.

This program targets Java 8 without preview flags. Use a full JDK for compiler-based examples.

A marker needs a consumer

A source annotation records an endpoint path, but the annotation itself does not validate that path. The processor reads the annotated type and emits an error when the value does not begin with a slash. That turns a declaration rule into a compiler check rather than a comment that reviewers must remember.

The program supplies the processor explicitly through the JavaCompiler API. It runs processing only against in-memory source units. No provider discovery or generated-source packaging is implied; command-line builds need their own processor registration and processor-path configuration.

Respect processing rounds and diagnostics

A processor can be called over multiple rounds. It should claim only annotation types that it owns, and avoid generating the same file repeatedly. This fixture does not generate files. It rejects one annotated type and accepts another, then checks the compiler task result instead of searching human-formatted diagnostic text.

Processing code runs with the build process privileges. A downloaded processor is executable build-time code, even if its dependency is described as tooling. Keep processor versions and inputs reviewable. A full JDK is required here because ToolProvider may not supply a compiler in a reduced runtime.

Working program

import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;
import java.net.URI;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.Set;
import javax.annotation.processing.AbstractProcessor;
import javax.annotation.processing.RoundEnvironment;
import javax.lang.model.SourceVersion;
import javax.lang.model.element.TypeElement;
import javax.tools.Diagnostic;
import javax.tools.DiagnosticCollector;
import javax.tools.JavaCompiler;
import javax.tools.JavaFileObject;
import javax.tools.SimpleJavaFileObject;
import javax.tools.StandardJavaFileManager;
import javax.tools.ToolProvider;
public class CompilerRouteAudit {
    @Target(ElementType.TYPE) @Retention(RetentionPolicy.SOURCE)
    public @interface Route { String value(); }
    static class RouteProcessor extends AbstractProcessor {
        public Set<String> getSupportedAnnotationTypes() { return Collections.singleton(Route.class.getCanonicalName()); }
        public SourceVersion getSupportedSourceVersion() { return SourceVersion.latestSupported(); }
        public boolean process(Set<? extends TypeElement> annotations, RoundEnvironment round) {
            for (javax.lang.model.element.Element endpoint : round.getElementsAnnotatedWith(Route.class))
                if (!endpoint.getAnnotation(Route.class).value().startsWith("/"))
                    processingEnv.getMessager().printMessage(Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR, "Route must start with a slash", endpoint);
            return true;
        }
    }
    static boolean check(String path) throws Exception {
        JavaCompiler compiler = ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler();
        if (compiler == null) throw new IllegalStateException("Full JDK required");
        String text = "@CompilerRouteAudit.Route(\""+path+"\") class ReceiptEndpoint {}";
        JavaFileObject unit = new SimpleJavaFileObject(URI.create("string:///ReceiptEndpoint.java"), JavaFileObject.Kind.SOURCE) {
            public CharSequence getCharContent(boolean ignoreErrors) { return text; }
        };
        DiagnosticCollector<JavaFileObject> diagnostics = new DiagnosticCollector<>();
        try (StandardJavaFileManager files = compiler.getStandardFileManager(diagnostics, null, null)) {
            JavaCompiler.CompilationTask task = compiler.getTask(null, files, diagnostics,
                java.util.Arrays.asList("-proc:only", "-classpath", System.getProperty("java.class.path")),
                null, Collections.singletonList(unit));
            task.setProcessors(Collections.singletonList(new RouteProcessor()));
            return task.call();
        }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println(check("/receipts")); System.out.println(check("receipts"));
    }
}

Output

true
false

Costs and boundaries

Processing work follows the number of compiler elements visited and any generated output. This processor scans its annotated types once per relevant round and generates nothing. It validates only the slash prefix; uniqueness, HTTP behavior and a complete routing grammar are separate application checks. The compiler runs inside this test process without compiling arbitrary user submissions.

Common Mistakes

  • Declaring an annotation does not automatically run a processor.
  • Do not regenerate the same source file in every round.
  • A compile-time syntax check does not establish runtime endpoint behavior.

title: Java LongAdder: striped counters and the limits of sum snapshots
summary: LongAdder distributes concurrent additions across internal counters and combines their values when sum is requested.
body:
LongAdder distributes concurrent additions across internal counters and combines their values when sum is requested.

This program targets Java 8 without preview flags. Use a full JDK for compiler-based examples.

Count observations, not remaining capacity

A parser can record how many rows workers accepted. Several workers increment the same metric, then the coordinator joins all workers and reports the count. A striped counter fits an observation metric because callers do not need to claim the next unique value or atomically reject a quota overrun.

The program waits until every writer has ended before reading the total. During concurrent updates, sum does not promise an atomic snapshot. Using it in a check-then-increment admission rule can allow more callers than the permitted capacity. An atomic transition or a semaphore is a different contract.

Reset needs an ownership rule

sumThenReset is useful only when a non-atomic reset is acceptable under the application timing rule. It is not a substitute for a precisely bounded reporting interval with active writers. Resetting a live metric and publishing it as an exact count can lose the connection between requests and windows.

The runtime chooses its internal stripe arrangement. This fixture proves the final arithmetic result after joins, not a throughput improvement over AtomicLong on every machine. False sharing, contention, processor count and read frequency all affect a real comparison.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder;
public class AcceptedRowMetric {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        LongAdder accepted = new LongAdder();
        Thread[] writers = new Thread[4];
        for (int index=0; index<writers.length; index++) {
            writers[index] = new Thread(() -> { for (int row=0; row<750; row++) accepted.increment(); });
            writers[index].start();
        }
        for (Thread writer : writers) writer.join();
        System.out.println(accepted.sum());
        System.out.println(accepted.sumThenReset());
        System.out.println(accepted.sum());
    }
}

Output

3000
3000
0

Costs and boundaries

Each increment performs bounded counter work but its contention cost is runtime-dependent. sum visits internal counter state and may cost more than reading one AtomicLong. This fixture retains four worker threads and one counter. It does not publish a timing comparison or justify replacing every application counter with LongAdder.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not use sum as an atomic quota decision while writers are active.
  • Do not assume reset creates an exact reporting window under concurrent updates.
  • The final count requires completion of all writers before observation.

title: Java ZIP inputs: bounded staging and rejected path traversal
summary: A ZIP entry name is untrusted input; before writing it, an extractor must establish that its destination remains inside the owned output directory.
body:
A ZIP entry name is untrusted input; before writing it, an extractor must establish that its destination remains inside the owned output directory.

This program targets Java 8 without preview flags. Use a full JDK for compiler-based examples.

Normalize a destination, not just a string prefix

A receipt archive can contain a name such as ../outside.txt. Concatenating that name with an output directory can escape the intended location. Resolve the entry against the root, normalize the resulting Path, and compare path components with startsWith; a string prefix comparison can confuse sibling directories.

This fixture rejects absolute names, backslashes, colons, empty names, root-only destinations and paths that normalize outside the root. It stages bytes in memory and does not write them to the file system. Restricting the accepted name grammar makes the lexical policy reproducible across the operating systems used by this example.

Compressed size is not the work budget

The header size may be absent or misleading. Count bytes as they are read and stop when the total uncompressed budget is exceeded. The program permits at most eight files and 64 KiB total output, and rejects duplicate normalized destinations before publication.

A lexical check does not settle symbolic-link races in a pre-existing directory. A production extractor needs an owned private staging directory, a policy for links and permissions, and a publication rule that cannot redirect writes between validation and creation. No general-purpose secure extraction guarantee is made by this in-memory example.

Working program

import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream;
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry;
import java.util.zip.ZipInputStream;
import java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream;
public class ReceiptArchiveStaging {
    static Map<Path, byte[]> stage(byte[] archive) throws Exception {
        Path root = Paths.get("receipt-output").toAbsolutePath().normalize();
        Map<Path, byte[]> staged = new LinkedHashMap<>(); int total=0;
        try (ZipInputStream input = new ZipInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(archive))) {
            ZipEntry entry;
            while ((entry=input.getNextEntry()) != null) {
                String name=entry.getName();
                if (name.isEmpty() || name.startsWith("/") || name.contains("\\") || name.contains(":")) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid name");
                Path target=root.resolve(name).normalize();
                if (!target.startsWith(root) || target.equals(root)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Outside root");
                if (entry.isDirectory()) { input.closeEntry(); continue; }
                if (staged.size()==8 || staged.containsKey(target)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("File count or duplicate");
                ByteArrayOutputStream content=new ByteArrayOutputStream(); byte[] buffer=new byte[1024]; int count;
                while ((count=input.read(buffer)) != -1) {
                    if (count>65536-total) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Uncompressed budget");
                    total+=count; content.write(buffer,0,count);
                }
                staged.put(target,content.toByteArray()); input.closeEntry();
            }
        }
        return staged;
    }
    static byte[] archive(String name) throws Exception {
        ByteArrayOutputStream bytes=new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        try (ZipOutputStream output=new ZipOutputStream(bytes)) {
            output.putNextEntry(new ZipEntry(name)); output.write("R-51".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); output.closeEntry();
        }
        return bytes.toByteArray();
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println(stage(archive("reports/receipt.txt")).size());
        try { stage(archive("../outside.txt")); }
        catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) { System.out.println("traversal rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

1
traversal rejected

Costs and boundaries

Decompression work depends on input and output bytes; staging retains at most 64 KiB of payload plus bounded path and buffer overhead. The caller must also bound compressed input before passing a byte array. This sample does not model encrypted archives, filesystem links, concurrent directory changes or crash-durable publication.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not validate destinations using string prefixes.
  • Do not trust ZIP header size as the decompression budget.
  • Do not publish partial files before validating the complete archive.

title: Java Clock: test expiry without sleeping
summary: A Clock supplies instants and a time zone so application code can read time through an explicit dependency instead of a hidden system call.
body:
A Clock supplies instants and a time zone so application code can read time through an explicit dependency instead of a hidden system call.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Define the expiry boundary

A payment reservation expires at a stored Instant. The predicate uses now greater than or equal to expiry. Equality matters: switching to a strict greater-than comparison grants an extra instant at the boundary. That is a business decision, not a formatting preference.

Use an instant for an absolute deadline. A LocalDateTime has no offset and cannot identify a unique point on the timeline during an overlap. Inject the clock into the service constructor; tests can then use a fixed instant without waiting or changing machine time.

Separate civil time from elapsed time

Clock.fixed returns the supplied instant whenever read. Clock.offset moves that view by a duration, which lets this fixture check both sides of an expiry boundary using the same reservation. Neither object simulates an operating system clock that ticks by itself.

For measuring elapsed latency inside one JVM, a monotonic time source such as System.nanoTime addresses a different problem. Wall time can change after synchronization. Do not use a fixed clock to conclude that concurrent timing or scheduler behavior has been tested.

Working program

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
public class ReservationExpiry {
    private final Clock clock;
    ReservationExpiry(Clock clock) { this.clock = clock; }
    boolean expired(Instant deadline) { return !clock.instant().isBefore(deadline); }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Instant deadline = Instant.parse("2026-01-12T12:00:00Z");
        Clock boundary = Clock.fixed(deadline, ZoneOffset.UTC);
        System.out.println(new ReservationExpiry(Clock.offset(boundary, Duration.ofSeconds(-1))).expired(deadline));
        System.out.println(new ReservationExpiry(boundary).expired(deadline));
    }
}

Output

false
true

Costs and boundaries

Each comparison is bounded work with constant application state. Storage precision can truncate timestamps, so test after converting to the database precision used in production. This fixture has no database and cannot establish that conversion contract.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not scatter Instant.now() through a service that needs reproducible tests.
  • Choose whether equality means expired.
  • A wall clock is not a monotonic latency counter.

title: Java daylight-saving transitions: reject gaps and choose overlaps
summary: A ZoneRules instance maps local date-time values to valid offsets; a gap has no valid offset and an overlap can have two.
body:
A ZoneRules instance maps local date-time values to valid offsets; a gap has no valid offset and an overlap can have two.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

A local appointment is not yet an instant

A scheduler accepting a local appointment needs a region zone and a rule for daylight-saving changes. Automatically adjusting a nonexistent time can move a booking away from what the customer entered. Reject it when the application contract requires an exact local time.

This fixture uses known 2024 transitions in Europe/Paris. The March appointment has no matching offset. The October appointment has two, and each creates a different Instant from the same local fields. The region rules come from the runtime time-zone database; governments can change future rules.

Make the overlap policy visible

An offset is a numeric displacement, not a region rule. Persist the selected instant and the region when both execution and later display matter. If a future appointment must stay at a civil time even after a rule change, store that civil intent separately and define when it is recalculated.

The program displays both overlap instants rather than silently selecting one. A production input flow should ask for or clearly specify the earlier or later offset. A blanket UTC conversion before examining the local-time ambiguity loses evidence the service needs to make that choice.

Working program

import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.List;
public class AppointmentOffsets {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of("Europe/Paris");
        LocalDateTime gap = LocalDateTime.parse("2024-03-31T02:30:00");
        LocalDateTime overlap = LocalDateTime.parse("2024-10-27T02:30:00");
        System.out.println("gap offsets=" + zone.getRules().getValidOffsets(gap).size());
        List<ZoneOffset> offsets = zone.getRules().getValidOffsets(overlap);
        System.out.println("overlap offsets=" + offsets.size());
        for (ZoneOffset offset : offsets) System.out.println(overlap.toInstant(offset));
    }
}

Output

gap offsets=0
overlap offsets=2
2024-10-27T00:30:00Z
2024-10-27T01:30:00Z

Costs and boundaries

The fixture stores at most two offsets per query. Region rules and their cached data are runtime resources; do not model them as a fixed application-owned lookup table for every future date.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat LocalDateTime as a unique instant.
  • A fixed ZoneOffset does not include regional daylight-saving rules.
  • Test gaps and overlaps separately.

title: Java Optional: eager defaults and lazy suppliers
summary: Optional.orElse evaluates its argument before the call, while orElseGet invokes its supplier only when the Optional is empty.
body:
Optional.orElse evaluates its argument before the call, while orElseGet invokes its supplier only when the Optional is empty.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

An unused default can still do work

A receipt lookup already found a cached value. Passing a fallback method to orElse does not postpone that method; Java evaluates the method argument even though Optional later returns the cached value. The fallback could allocate a document, query a database or fail.

The counter in this program records actual fallback calls. It is intentionally local and deterministic. orElseGet avoids the call on a present value, but writing a supplier that closes over an already-computed fallback will not undo the earlier computation.

Absence is a domain choice

A supplier can return null, so the return value of orElseGet is not automatically non-null. If absence is an error, orElseThrow can express that boundary directly. Avoid using Optional merely to hide a missing value that the caller must handle explicitly.

The fixture uses a single thread. Adding suppliers with mutable shared counters needs synchronization, and deferring a remote lookup still needs a timeout and failure policy. Lazy evaluation controls when work starts; it does not make the work safe or inexpensive.

Working program

import java.util.Optional;
public class ReceiptFallbackCalls {
    static int calls;
    static String loadArchive() { calls++; return "archive"; }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Optional<String> receipt = Optional.of("cached");
        System.out.println(receipt.orElse(loadArchive()));
        System.out.println(calls);
        System.out.println(receipt.orElseGet(ReceiptFallbackCalls::loadArchive));
        System.out.println(calls);
        System.out.println(Optional.<String>empty().orElseGet(ReceiptFallbackCalls::loadArchive));
        System.out.println(calls);
    }
}

Output

cached
1
cached
1
archive
2

Costs and boundaries

Optional selection itself is bounded work. The fallback cost depends on the operation supplied. Captured state can keep objects reachable longer than expected; a supplier is not a free replacement for designing the lookup lifecycle.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not assume an orElse argument is lazy.
  • Do not compute the fallback before creating its supplier.
  • Handle exceptions from the supplier at the intended boundary.

title: Java Spliterator: split traversal without inventing characteristics
summary: A Spliterator traverses elements and may partition the remaining traversal; its characteristic flags describe promises about that source.
body:
A Spliterator traverses elements and may partition the remaining traversal; its characteristic flags describe promises about that source.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Split the remaining work

A receipt batch is an ordered list. trySplit hands out a portion of the unvisited elements while leaving the rest on the original spliterator. Consume both parts to cover the batch. Consuming only the original after a successful split loses the elements transferred to the returned object.

This program checks the sum after consuming both parts; it does not assume a particular split size. A spliterator may return null, so callers must still consume the original when partitioning is unavailable. Splitting alone does not create threads or schedule tasks.

Flags are contracts

ORDERED does not mean sorted. SIZED means the estimate is exact under its contract; SUBSIZED extends the size promise to splits. A custom spliterator that declares an unsupported property can cause downstream operations to rely on evidence it did not supply.

The fixture avoids source mutation during traversal. Fail-fast detection is not a concurrency protocol. A parallel stream also needs independent operations and a suitable source; adding parallel() to a shared mutable accumulator creates a separate correctness problem.

Working program

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Spliterator;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
public class PartitionedReceiptAmounts {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Spliterator<Integer> remaining = Arrays.asList(12, 18, 25, 45).spliterator();
        Spliterator<Integer> prefix = remaining.trySplit();
        AtomicInteger total = new AtomicInteger();
        if (prefix != null) prefix.forEachRemaining(total::addAndGet);
        remaining.forEachRemaining(total::addAndGet);
        System.out.println(total.get());
        System.out.println(remaining.hasCharacteristics(Spliterator.ORDERED));
    }
}

Output

100
true

Costs and boundaries

Traversal visits n elements in O(n) time. The sequential example keeps bounded accumulator state; the source list stores n elements. Actual split costs depend on the source, and a linked structure can partition differently from an array-backed one.

Common Mistakes

  • Consume both returned and remaining partitions.
  • Do not label unsorted data SORTED.
  • Splitting is not thread execution.

title: Java toMap: reject or merge duplicate keys deliberately
summary: Collectors.toMap accumulates stream elements into a map, and a duplicate key needs either an explicit merge rule or a visible failure.
body:
Collectors.toMap accumulates stream elements into a map, and a duplicate key needs either an explicit merge rule or a visible failure.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Choose what duplicate means

Two receipt rows share a currency code. If the target represents total exposure per currency, summing amounts is appropriate. If the target represents one authoritative payment per identifier, keeping the first row would conceal inconsistent input. The merge function belongs to the domain contract.

The program first verifies that the two-argument collector rejects a duplicate, then supplies a sum rule and a TreeMap factory for reproducible key order. It uses checked integer addition so overflow is rejected rather than wrapping silently.

Parallel reduction adds another constraint

A merge function used in parallel reduction must produce the intended result under grouping changes. Subtracting values in the merge function is not a valid substitute for adding them. Side effects on another map or counter also introduce ordering and concurrency dependencies.

The fixture contains positive bounded amounts. Real currency calculations need a documented unit and rounding rule, often BigDecimal or a checked integral minor-unit value. A collection operation does not validate currency scale or convert between currencies.

Working program

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
public class CurrencyExposure {
    static class Row {
        final String currency; final int minorUnits;
        Row(String currency, int minorUnits) { this.currency = currency; this.minorUnits = minorUnits; }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Row> rows = Arrays.asList(new Row("INR", 120), new Row("INR", 80), new Row("USD", 50));
        try { rows.stream().collect(Collectors.toMap(row -> row.currency, row -> row.minorUnits)); }
        catch (IllegalStateException rejected) { System.out.println("duplicate rejected"); }
        Map<String,Integer> totals = rows.stream().collect(Collectors.toMap(
            row -> row.currency, row -> row.minorUnits, Math::addExact, TreeMap::new));
        System.out.println(totals);
    }
}

Output

duplicate rejected
{INR=200, USD=50}

Costs and boundaries

TreeMap insertion costs O(log k) for k distinct keys, so this collector uses O(n log k) time and O(k) map storage. The ordinary hash-map form has a different cost profile. Sorting is chosen for deterministic output, not claimed as a faster collector.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not silently overwrite an identifier that should be unique.
  • Make the merge function suitable for the reduction grouping.
  • Define money units before summing.

title: Java Stream.close: terminal traversal does not close every source
summary: A Stream can have a close handler, but a terminal operation does not by itself invoke that handler.
body:
A Stream can have a close handler, but a terminal operation does not by itself invoke that handler.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Traversal and resource release are different events

A file-backed stream can hold a reader while elements are processed. Reaching count() or collecting the values is not a general resource-release protocol. Close the stream with try-with-resources when its source owns an external resource.

This fixture uses Stream.of and an onClose counter rather than opening a file, making the lifecycle distinction visible without depending on filesystem state. The count completes while the close counter remains zero; leaving the try block changes it to one.

Do not return ownership ambiguously

A helper that returns a file-backed stream transfers a resource obligation to its caller. Document that obligation or collect the required bounded data inside the helper and close it there. Collecting an unbounded input is not a safe way to avoid documenting ownership.

A stream is single-use. Closing one also prevents later traversal, and exceptions in processing still require release. If traversal and closing both fail, try-with-resources records the closing failure as suppressed rather than replacing the original failure.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
public class ReceiptStreamLifetime {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        AtomicInteger closed = new AtomicInteger();
        try (Stream<String> receiptIds = Stream.of("R-21", "R-22").onClose(closed::incrementAndGet)) {
            System.out.println(receiptIds.count());
            System.out.println("before close=" + closed.get());
        }
        System.out.println("after close=" + closed.get());
    }
}

Output

2
before close=0
after close=1

Costs and boundaries

The example uses constant application state and a two-element source. A real lazy source can bound memory while still keeping descriptors open; memory usage and descriptor lifetime require separate checks.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not assume collect() closes a Files.lines stream.
  • Do not return a resource-backed stream without explaining who closes it.
  • Do not reuse a consumed stream.

title: Java ThreadLocal: clear request state on reused worker threads
summary: A ThreadLocal stores a value associated with a thread, so a pool worker can retain that value after the request that set it finishes.
body:
A ThreadLocal stores a value associated with a thread, so a pool worker can retain that value after the request that set it finishes.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

A pool changes the lifetime

A request identifier is useful for local logging, but a pooled thread normally lives longer than one request. If cleanup is skipped, the next task can observe the previous identifier. The error is an ownership mismatch: request state was stored in worker-owned storage.

This program uses a single-thread executor to make worker reuse deterministic. The first task installs an identifier and removes it in finally; the second task reads null. Clearing only on a successful path leaves stale state when processing throws.

Context does not travel automatically

ThreadLocal values are not a transaction or an authorization mechanism. Moving work to another executor does not automatically transfer the intended value, and blindly copying context can transfer credentials beyond their lifetime. Pass ordinary arguments when that ownership is easier to inspect.

The fixture waits for each Future and shuts down its executor. It tests cleanup, not every interleaving in a multi-worker pool. A production wrapper should restore an earlier value when nested operations share a thread, rather than always destroying another caller’s context.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
public class RequestContextCleanup {
    static final ThreadLocal<String> REQUEST = new ThreadLocal<>();
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        ExecutorService worker = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor();
        try {
            System.out.println(worker.submit(() -> {
                REQUEST.set("receipt-71");
                try { return REQUEST.get(); }
                finally { REQUEST.remove(); }
            }).get());
            System.out.println(worker.submit(() -> REQUEST.get()).get());
        } finally { worker.shutdownNow(); }
    }
}

Output

receipt-71
null

Costs and boundaries

One value is stored per participating thread while the context exists. A large object stored there can remain reachable through a long-lived worker. remove() releases this thread’s association, but it does not erase copies of the data held elsewhere.

Common Mistakes

  • Place cleanup in finally.
  • Do not treat thread-local values as authenticated identity.
  • Account for nested context and restore an existing value when needed.

title: Java bounded executors: test saturation and rejected work
summary: A ThreadPoolExecutor with a bounded queue can reject a submitted task when its workers and queue cannot accept more work.
body:
A ThreadPoolExecutor with a bounded queue can reject a submitted task when its workers and queue cannot accept more work.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Backlog needs a limit

An importer with one worker and one queue slot can hold one running task and one waiting task. A third submission must meet an explicit rejection rule. An unbounded queue changes the failure mode to growing memory and delay; it does not create extra processing capacity.

The fixture blocks the worker on a latch, fills the queue, and checks AbortPolicy rejection. It then releases the worker in finally. That arrangement controls saturation without relying on sleeps or guessing how quickly a worker starts.

Choose what the caller observes

CallerRunsPolicy moves execution onto the submitting thread, which can slow admission but may also block an HTTP request or event-loop thread. Silently discarding a task can lose work while the caller believes it was accepted. Neither policy is universally correct.

A queue limit does not supply durable storage. If the JVM exits, queued work disappears. A service that promises eventual processing needs persistence and replay semantics outside this local executor demonstration.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.ArrayBlockingQueue;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException;
import java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
public class ImportAdmission {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        CountDownLatch release = new CountDownLatch(1);
        ThreadPoolExecutor worker = new ThreadPoolExecutor(1, 1, 0, TimeUnit.SECONDS,
            new ArrayBlockingQueue<Runnable>(1), new ThreadPoolExecutor.AbortPolicy());
        try {
            worker.execute(() -> { try { release.await(); } catch (InterruptedException stop) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); } });
            worker.execute(() -> {});
            try { worker.execute(() -> {}); }
            catch (RejectedExecutionException rejected) { System.out.println("capacity rejected"); }
            System.out.println("queued=" + worker.getQueue().size());
        } finally { release.countDown(); worker.shutdown(); }
        if (!worker.awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) throw new AssertionError("worker did not stop");
    }
}

Output

capacity rejected
queued=1

Costs and boundaries

This queue holds at most one task and the pool has one worker. Retained task closures can still reference large payloads, so a bounded task count is not an exact byte budget. This test checks admission and termination, not production throughput.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not hide rejected work behind a success response.
  • Bound payload size as well as queue length.
  • Release test latches even when an assertion fails.

title: Java SecureRandom: token entropy, encoding and comparison boundaries
summary: SecureRandom produces bytes from a cryptographic random generator; a token format must preserve those bytes and define its own validation rules.
body:
SecureRandom produces bytes from a cryptographic random generator; a token format must preserve those bytes and define its own validation rules.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Count bytes before formatting

This fixture generates 24 bytes and encodes them with unpadded URL-safe Base64. Twenty-four bytes represent 192 bits of raw random input. That number does not prove an entire authentication scheme is secure: token storage, expiry, transmission and lookup behavior remain separate requirements.

The output check uses the decoded byte count rather than a fixed token string. Tests should never expect a particular random value or seed a production token generator merely to make a screenshot reproducible.

Do not compare the wrong representation

Encoding is reversible; it does not hash or encrypt a token. Validate the transport format before decoding and handle malformed input as rejected input. When comparing secret byte strings of an expected length, MessageDigest.isEqual is preferable to writing an early-exit byte loop.

The fixture compares a token to its own decoded bytes, which verifies a round trip only. It does not implement login, token rotation or rate limiting. A database should avoid storing bearer credentials in readable form where a lookup digest can meet the design requirements.

Working program

import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.security.SecureRandom;
import java.util.Base64;
public class OpaqueReceiptToken {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        byte[] entropy = new byte[24];
        new SecureRandom().nextBytes(entropy);
        String encoded = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(entropy);
        byte[] decoded = Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(encoded);
        System.out.println("characters=" + encoded.length());
        System.out.println("bytes=" + decoded.length);
        System.out.println(MessageDigest.isEqual(entropy, decoded));
    }
}

Output

characters=32
bytes=24
true

Costs and boundaries

Generation and encoding scale with token length; this fixed fixture uses bounded buffers. Provider initialization can have different costs from later calls. Benchmark the actual generator and deployment rather than treating a tiny example as a latency guarantee.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not use Random for bearer token generation.
  • Base64 is not encryption.
  • Never log the generated credential as routine diagnostic data.

title: Java segment tree: range sums with checked updates
summary: A segment tree stores aggregate values over nested intervals so a point update and a range-sum query can each visit logarithmically many nodes.
body:
A segment tree stores aggregate values over nested intervals so a point update and a range-sum query can each visit logarithmically many nodes.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

Use one interval convention

A stock ledger needs the total quantity for a contiguous range of warehouse slots after individual corrections. This implementation uses half-open intervals: start is included and end is excluded. An empty range returns zero; a reversed or out-of-bounds range is rejected.

The tree uses an iterative layout with leaves starting at index n. It does not require n to be a power of two for this sum query. Parent values are rebuilt from child sums. Long storage prevents ordinary int-sum overflow for this bounded fixture, but arbitrary long inputs still need an overflow policy.

Update ownership is local

An update replaces one leaf rather than adding a delta, then recomputes its ancestors. A caller that mistakes replacement for increment will get plausible but incorrect totals. The test changes one warehouse from five to nine and checks the new sum.

This class is not thread-safe. A concurrent query can observe part of an update. Protect the complete tree operation with a lock or choose a versioned structure when readers need a consistent snapshot; marking the array reference volatile does not make its element mutations atomic as a group.

Working program

public class WarehouseRangeTotals {
    private final int size; private final long[] tree;
    WarehouseRangeTotals(int[] quantities) {
        size = quantities.length;
        if (size == 0 || size > 1000000) throw new IllegalArgumentException("size");
        tree = new long[2 * size];
        for (int index = 0; index < size; index++) tree[size + index] = quantities[index];
        for (int node = size - 1; node > 0; node--) tree[node] = tree[2 * node] + tree[2 * node + 1];
    }
    void replace(int index, int value) {
        if (index < 0 || index >= size) throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException();
        int node = index + size; tree[node] = value;
        while ((node /= 2) > 0) tree[node] = tree[2 * node] + tree[2 * node + 1];
    }
    long sum(int start, int end) {
        if (start < 0 || end < start || end > size) throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException();
        long total = 0;
        for (int left = start + size, right = end + size; left < right; left /= 2, right /= 2) {
            if ((left & 1) != 0) total += tree[left++];
            if ((right & 1) != 0) total += tree[--right];
        }
        return total;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        WarehouseRangeTotals stock = new WarehouseRangeTotals(new int[]{3, 5, 2, 7, 4});
        System.out.println(stock.sum(1, 4));
        stock.replace(1, 9); System.out.println(stock.sum(1, 4));
        System.out.println(stock.sum(2, 2));
        try { stock.sum(4, 2); } catch (IndexOutOfBoundsException rejected) { System.out.println("range rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

14
18
0
range rejected

Costs and boundaries

Construction is O(n), queries and point replacements are O(log n), and the array stores 2n long values. This version supports sums and point replacement only; lazy range updates need different state and are not implemented here.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not mix inclusive and half-open endpoints.
  • Point replacement is not a delta update.
  • Protect a whole mutation when concurrent snapshots matter.

title: Java minimum coin change: reachable states and impossible totals
summary: Minimum coin change uses earlier reachable amounts to compute the smallest number of reusable denominations that can form a target total.
body:
Minimum coin change uses earlier reachable amounts to compute the smallest number of reusable denominations that can form a target total.

The complete program targets Java 8. Compile it as one source file; its output is checked against the lesson.

An unreachable state is not zero

A voucher issuer supports denominations three and five. It must find the minimum voucher count for an exact total, or report that no combination exists. Initializing every state to zero would make nonexistent predecessor states look like free money.

The recurrence starts at zero vouchers for total zero and marks other totals unreachable. For each total it considers every denomination that fits. The resulting state represents exact totals with unlimited reuse of the supplied positive denominations.

Input bounds are part of the algorithm

A denomination of zero creates a self-dependency and a negative one violates the recurrence. Reject both. The target is capped at one million to bound allocation and prevent target-plus-one overflow in this implementation.

This is not a greedy algorithm. Choosing the largest denomination first can miss a better combination or fail when a smaller-first combination exists. A bounded supply of each denomination is another problem and needs a count-sensitive state transition.

Working program

import java.util.Arrays;
public class VoucherMinimum {
    static int minimum(int[] denominations, int target) {
        if (target < 0 || target > 1000000 || denominations.length == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("target or coins");
        for (int coin : denominations) if (coin <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("coin");
        int missing = target + 1;
        int[] best = new int[target + 1]; Arrays.fill(best, missing); best[0] = 0;
        for (int amount = 1; amount <= target; amount++) {
            for (int coin : denominations) if (coin <= amount && best[amount - coin] != missing)
                best[amount] = Math.min(best[amount], best[amount - coin] + 1);
        }
        return best[target] == missing ? -1 : best[target];
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(minimum(new int[]{3, 5}, 11));
        System.out.println(minimum(new int[]{3, 5}, 4));
        System.out.println(minimum(new int[]{3, 5}, 0));
        try { minimum(new int[]{0, 5}, 9); } catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) { System.out.println("coin rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

3
-1
0
coin rejected

Costs and boundaries

For target t and k denominations the running time is O(tk) and state storage is O(t). Duplicate denominations repeat work without changing the optimum. The code returns the count only; reconstructing an actual voucher list needs predecessor information.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not initialize unreachable amounts as zero.
  • Reject non-positive denominations.
  • Unlimited reuse and bounded inventory need different transitions.

title: Java UTF-8 decoding: reject malformed bytes before parsing
summary: A CharsetDecoder converts bytes to characters and can report malformed input instead of replacing it silently.
body:
A CharsetDecoder converts bytes to characters and can report malformed input instead of replacing it silently.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Preserve the evidence

A receipt import accepts UTF-8 bytes, not arbitrary platform text. The input contract rejects an incomplete multibyte sequence. A convenience String constructor can replace bad bytes, leaving a character sequence that looks valid enough for a later parser while no longer matching what arrived. Decode first. Validate the resulting fields separately.

The fixture sends one ordinary amount record and one truncated sequence through the same decoder policy. It reports rejection without printing a payload that could contain personal data. This is a byte-level contract; it does not validate the record schema, numeric range or identity of the sender.

A decoder has state

Create a decoder per independent operation or manage its reset lifecycle explicitly. Decoder instances are mutable and should not be shared by concurrent requests. The one-shot decode method handles the end of the supplied buffer; incremental imports need an explicit final decode and flush while retaining incomplete bytes between chunks.

Cap the incoming bytes before decoding. Checking character count afterward does not prevent allocating an enormous byte buffer. A streaming reader can bound retained memory, but its chunk boundaries must not be mistaken for character boundaries. Encoding rules and HTTP field validation handle different layers.

Working program

import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.charset.*;
public class ReceiptUtf8Boundary {
    static String decode(byte[] bytes) throws CharacterCodingException {
        if (bytes.length > 4096) throw new IllegalArgumentException("record too large");
        return StandardCharsets.UTF_8.newDecoder()
            .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPORT)
            .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPORT)
            .decode(ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes)).toString();
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println(decode("amount=125".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)));
        try { decode(new byte[]{(byte)0xE2, (byte)0x82}); }
        catch (CharacterCodingException rejected) { System.out.println("malformed rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

amount=125
malformed rejected

Costs and boundaries

For b input bytes, this one-shot conversion takes O(b) time and O(b) character storage in the worst case. The 4096-byte limit applies to this record format, not every import. Separate parsing and authentication costs remain outside the decoder.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not use replacement decoding for an import that must reject corrupted bytes.
  • Do not share one mutable decoder across threads.
  • Bound bytes before allocating the full payload.

title: Java strict date parsing: reject impossible calendar input
summary: A DateTimeFormatter with STRICT resolution rejects invalid calendar combinations rather than adjusting them to a valid date.
body:
A DateTimeFormatter with STRICT resolution rejects invalid calendar combinations rather than adjusting them to a valid date.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

A parsed shape is not a valid date

A delivery request sends an ISO-shaped local date. Four digits, a dash and two numeric fields are insufficient: 29 February must be checked against the selected year. The fixture accepts the leap-year date and rejects the same day in a non-leap year. That distinction belongs at the request boundary.

Use uuuu for a proleptic year in this formatter. yyyy denotes year-of-era and can need an era to resolve under strict rules. A convenient formatter that normalizes an impossible day can move a booking away from the value a person submitted.

Dates do not contain deadlines

A LocalDate has no time or offset. Converting it to a deadline requires a zone and a rule for which instant ends the allowed period. Zone gaps and overlaps are separate from calendar validity, and a valid local date does not resolve them.

The immutable formatter can be reused. Do not replace it with a shared mutable legacy date parser. Exception messages may include user input; a public API should return a bounded error contract rather than exposing its entire parsing exception. Problem details supplies that response boundary.

Working program

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.format.*;
import java.util.Locale;
public class DeliveryDateInput {
    static final DateTimeFormatter INPUT = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("uuuu-MM-dd", Locale.ROOT)
        .withResolverStyle(ResolverStyle.STRICT);
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(LocalDate.parse("2024-02-29", INPUT));
        try { LocalDate.parse("2023-02-29", INPUT); }
        catch (DateTimeParseException rejected) { System.out.println("invalid day rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

2024-02-29
invalid day rejected

Costs and boundaries

Parsing takes time proportional to the bounded input length and returns one date object. The formatter can be shared because it is immutable. This program does not test time-zone conversion or a database date column.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not silently repair a booking date.
  • Use the year field that matches the intended resolution contract.
  • A valid LocalDate is not an absolute instant.

title: Java DecimalFormat: reject trailing input and pin the locale
summary: DecimalFormat parses locale-dependent numbers, and ParsePosition exposes how much of the input was consumed.
body:
DecimalFormat parses locale-dependent numbers, and ParsePosition exposes how much of the input was consumed.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Require the whole field

An invoice amount parser must reject 125.50INR when its contract accepts a numeric field only. DecimalFormat can parse a valid prefix, so getting a Number is weaker than validating the whole field. Check the final parse index against input length and reject an empty or failed parse.

The program fixes US symbols, disables grouping and requests BigDecimal output. It then applies scale two with UNNECESSARY rounding, making fractional precision a visible boundary. Locale-dependent punctuation is a user interface policy; a machine API should define its own numeric grammar.

Parsing is not complete domain validation

A positive amount and a finite scale still do not identify a currency. Store the currency or minor-unit contract separately. Locale data is not evidence that every textual variation is acceptable. If the input must match a narrow ASCII wire format, validate that grammar explicitly before DecimalFormat.

DecimalFormat is mutable. This fixture creates it locally rather than putting one parser in a singleton service. Shared parser reuse can turn a predictable format rule into a thread-safety problem. BigDecimal arithmetic handles later calculations; Typed configuration handles startup values.

Working program

import java.math.*;
import java.text.*;
import java.util.Locale;
public class InvoiceAmountInput {
    static BigDecimal parse(String input) {
        if (input.length() > 32) throw new IllegalArgumentException("amount too long");
        DecimalFormat format = new DecimalFormat("0.00", DecimalFormatSymbols.getInstance(Locale.US));
        format.setGroupingUsed(false); format.setParseBigDecimal(true);
        ParsePosition position = new ParsePosition(0);
        Number parsed = format.parse(input, position);
        if (!(parsed instanceof BigDecimal) || position.getIndex() != input.length())
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("complete decimal required");
        BigDecimal amount = ((BigDecimal) parsed).setScale(2, RoundingMode.UNNECESSARY);
        if (amount.signum() <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("positive amount required");
        return amount;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(parse("125.50"));
        try { parse("125.50INR"); }
        catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) { System.out.println("suffix rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

125.50
suffix rejected

Costs and boundaries

Parsing and BigDecimal allocation grow with the digit count, bounded here by 32 characters. Creating a local formatter avoids shared mutable state at an allocation cost. This parser deliberately does not implement every currency or strict ASCII notation.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat a valid prefix as a valid amount field.
  • Pin the locale instead of inheriting the machine default.
  • Do not share DecimalFormat without an ownership policy.

title: Java serialization filters: constrain classes and object graphs
summary: An ObjectInputFilter can reject deserialized classes and graph sizes before ObjectInputStream returns an object.
body:
An ObjectInputFilter can reject deserialized classes and graph sizes before ObjectInputStream returns an object.

This complete program targets Java 11. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Limit the specific legacy contract

A legacy migration file is expected to contain one small primitive int array. The fixture allows only int[] and caps its length, graph depth, references and reported bytes. It also caps the input byte array before opening the stream. A larger array and a different primitive array class are rejected independently.

This deliberately narrow filter has no application-defined serializable classes and no callbacks. Accepting an entire package would enlarge the trusted code surface. Prefer an explicit data format for new boundaries; a filter is a constraint on an existing serialization path, not a reason to accept arbitrary object streams.

Validate the returned value too

A filter receives graph information and sometimes no class. Return UNDECIDED for a metric-only callback after checking bounds, and reject unknown non-null classes. After reading, check the root type and application values. A class allowlist does not prove that an accepted array contains a valid business record.

The fixture checks complete locally generated files, not hostile network fuzzing. Stream metrics are not a substitute for a transport byte limit: filtering callbacks are not guaranteed to occur at every byte. Bounded byte input should be designed before the object stream is constructed.

Working program

import java.io.*;
public class LegacyBatchFilter {
    static byte[] encode(Object value) throws IOException {
        ByteArrayOutputStream bytes = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        try (ObjectOutputStream out = new ObjectOutputStream(bytes)) { out.writeObject(value); }
        return bytes.toByteArray();
    }
    static int[] read(byte[] bytes) throws Exception {
        if (bytes.length > 1024) throw new IOException("byte limit");
        try (ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes))) {
            in.setObjectInputFilter(info -> {
                if (info.depth() > 2 || info.references() > 8 || info.streamBytes() > 1024 || info.arrayLength() > 4)
                    return ObjectInputFilter.Status.REJECTED;
                Class<?> type = info.serialClass();
                return type == null ? ObjectInputFilter.Status.UNDECIDED
                    : type == int[].class ? ObjectInputFilter.Status.ALLOWED : ObjectInputFilter.Status.REJECTED;
            });
            Object value = in.readObject();
            if (!(value instanceof int[])) throw new IOException("root type");
            return (int[]) value;
        }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println(read(encode(new int[]{12, 18})).length);
        try { read(encode(new int[5])); }
        catch (InvalidClassException rejected) { System.out.println("length rejected"); }
        try { read(encode(new long[]{12})); }
        catch (InvalidClassException rejected) { System.out.println("class rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

2
length rejected
class rejected

Costs and boundaries

Serialization walks the accepted object graph and allocates reconstructed values. The fixture bounds the byte array and array length; it does not establish a universal CPU limit or sandbox code in accepted classes. Do not deserialize untrusted objects merely because a filter exists.

Common Mistakes

  • Avoid broad package allowlists for a narrow migration format.
  • Cap transport input independently of filter callbacks.
  • Validate the root and its values after reading.

title: Java shared Arena: coordinate access before closing memory
summary: A shared Arena permits multiple threads to access its memory segments while retaining an explicit lifetime that ends on close.
body:
A shared Arena permits multiple threads to access its memory segments while retaining an explicit lifetime that ends on close.

This complete program targets Java 25. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Sharing access does not order writes

The import worker writes one native-memory integer. The main thread joins that worker before reading and before closing the arena. The join supplies the ordering boundary. A shared arena removes thread confinement; it does not turn ordinary memory reads and writes into an application-level synchronization protocol.

The fixture chooses one writer and one reader rather than concurrent conflicting updates. Its segment remains inside the owner scope, and closing happens only after the worker completes. Passing a segment to an executor without tracking outstanding tasks would create a use-after-close path.

The owner closes after the users finish

Native storage is not Java heap storage. The segment object can stay reachable after its arena has been closed, but access through that segment then fails. This program retains the object only to check that failure, not to continue using released memory.

If a worker fails, joining still completes but the owner must inspect its failure before trusting the result. Larger import systems need an explicit task-completion and cancellation policy. Executor lifetime and Container cleanup connect to the same ownership question.

Working program

import java.lang.foreign.*;
public class SharedImportMemory {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        MemorySegment retained;
        try (Arena arena = Arena.ofShared()) {
            retained = arena.allocate(ValueLayout.JAVA_INT);
            Thread worker = new Thread(() -> retained.set(ValueLayout.JAVA_INT, 0, 125));
            worker.start(); worker.join();
            System.out.println(retained.get(ValueLayout.JAVA_INT, 0));
        }
        try { retained.get(ValueLayout.JAVA_INT, 0); }
        catch (IllegalStateException closed) { System.out.println("closed access rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

125
closed access rejected

Costs and boundaries

The fixture allocates one integer outside the Java heap plus a segment wrapper and one thread. Thread startup dominates this small operation. Larger buffers scale native memory with allocated bytes; a shared arena does not impose an import-size limit.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not close the arena while queued tasks still hold its segments.
  • Shared access does not prevent data races.
  • Handle worker failures before accepting their output.

title: Java Phaser: deregister workers so a phase can complete
summary: A Phaser coordinates a registered set of participants across numbered phases and permits participants to deregister.
body:
A Phaser coordinates a registered set of participants across numbered phases and permits participants to deregister.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Registration is a completion obligation

An import coordinator registers itself and two workers. Every registered party must arrive before the phase advances. A failed worker that leaves without arriving can keep the coordinator waiting forever. The fixture puts arrival and deregistration in finally so its registration is released even if work throws.

Register before starting the worker. Registering inside a thread can race with the coordinator arriving and advancing before the intended participant exists. The initial party count makes this fixture’s starting boundary explicit.

A barrier is not an error report

The workers increment a thread-safe completed counter. The barrier says both released their phase obligations; it does not say their business operations succeeded. Keep failures separately and inspect them after the phase when the task contract requires all records to pass.

This program waits without a timeout because its workers do bounded local work. Production coordination needs an interruption or deadline policy and a way to stop remaining tasks. Cancellation does not automatically roll back effects already committed by another worker.

Working program

import java.util.concurrent.Phaser;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
public class ImportPhaseCompletion {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Phaser phase = new Phaser(3);
        AtomicInteger completed = new AtomicInteger();
        Runnable task = () -> { try { completed.incrementAndGet(); } finally { phase.arriveAndDeregister(); } };
        Thread first = new Thread(task), second = new Thread(task);
        first.start(); second.start();
        phase.arriveAndAwaitAdvance();
        first.join(); second.join();
        System.out.println("completed=" + completed.get());
        System.out.println("remaining=" + phase.getRegisteredParties());
        phase.arriveAndDeregister();
        System.out.println("terminated=" + phase.isTerminated());
    }
}

Output

completed=2
remaining=1
terminated=true

Costs and boundaries

The coordinator stores participant counts rather than one result per participant. This fixture creates two threads and one counter. A barrier does not bound task duration, and retaining worker results or failures adds application storage proportional to the worker count.

Common Mistakes

  • Release registration in finally when a worker exits.
  • Register before work can race with phase advancement.
  • Do not interpret arrival as business success.

title: Java LinkedList ListIterator: edit at a cursor without repeated searches
summary: A ListIterator tracks a position between list elements and supports controlled insertion, replacement and removal during traversal.
body:
A ListIterator tracks a position between list elements and supports controlled insertion, replacement and removal during traversal.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Use the cursor as the edit location

A review queue contains Read, Code and Ship. The cursor moves over Read, inserts Test after it, then moves over Code and removes it. Insertion uses the cursor gap; removal uses the last element returned by traversal. The resulting queue is Read, Test, Ship.

After add, remove cannot be called until next or previous establishes a new last-returned element. The second part of the fixture checks that state rule explicitly. A cursor is more than an integer index: its allowed operations depend on the last traversal and edit.

Do not pay for a new search on every step

A loop that repeatedly calls get(index) on a linked list revisits nodes and can take quadratic total time. Once positioned, the iterator can traverse and edit without starting a new search for every element. Obtaining listIterator(index) can still require locating that position.

The fixture has one thread and edits through the iterator itself. External structural mutation invalidates its assumptions; best-effort fail-fast detection cannot protect a shared queue. For concurrent production work, choose the appropriate queue contract and define ownership rather than relying on an exception.

Working program

import java.util.*;
public class ReviewQueueCursor {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        LinkedList<String> queue = new LinkedList<>(Arrays.asList("Read", "Code", "Ship"));
        ListIterator<String> cursor = queue.listIterator();
        cursor.next(); cursor.add("Test"); cursor.next(); cursor.remove();
        System.out.println(queue);
        cursor.add("Audit");
        try { cursor.remove(); }
        catch (IllegalStateException rejected) { System.out.println("cursor state rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

[Read, Test, Ship]
cursor state rejected

Costs and boundaries

Walking n elements through one cursor takes O(n) time. Positioning at an arbitrary index can take O(n), while cursor-local node edits have constant structural work. Each stored element requires a linked node; this is not evidence that LinkedList beats an array-backed queue for the workload.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not call remove immediately after add without a traversal step.
  • Avoid indexed loops over a linked list.
  • Do not treat fail-fast detection as synchronization.

title: Java lazy segment tree: add to ranges and query sums
summary: A lazy segment tree records a deferred update on a covered interval so range additions do not visit every element immediately.
body:
A lazy segment tree records a deferred update on a covered interval so range additions do not visit every element immediately.

This complete program targets Java 8. Its displayed output is checked by the tutorial validation script.

Store both the aggregate and the deferred work

A capacity ledger needs to add the same reservation adjustment to every slot in an interval and read interval totals. Each tree node stores its sum and a pending addition for its descendants. Covering a node updates its sum by delta times interval length and records the deferred delta.

Before visiting part of a covered node, push its deferred addition to both children. Otherwise a later partial query reads old child sums even though the parent looks correct. Zero is the identity for an absent contribution, not a missing-value sentinel.

Specify the arithmetic boundary

The implementation accepts nonempty arrays up to 100000 elements and half-open intervals with at least one element. It uses long sums and requires callers to keep every intermediate sum and product within long range. The code does not detect overflow; wrapping invalidates the result. Production ledgers need an overflow or wider-number policy before using this model.

Queries can push deferred updates, so they mutate internal representation even though the logical values remain unchanged. Do not expose this tree to concurrent readers without synchronization. Compare it with point-update trees and Fenwick sums before choosing the state you need.

Working program

public class CapacityRangeTree {
    private final int count;
    private final long[] sums, pending;
    CapacityRangeTree(long[] values) {
        if (values.length == 0 || values.length > 100000) throw new IllegalArgumentException("size");
        count = values.length; sums = new long[4 * count]; pending = new long[4 * count];
        build(1, 0, count, values);
    }
    private void build(int node, int left, int right, long[] values) {
        if (right-left == 1) { sums[node] = values[left]; return; }
        int middle = left + (right-left)/2;
        build(node*2,left,middle,values); build(node*2+1,middle,right,values);
        sums[node] = sums[node*2] + sums[node*2+1];
    }
    private void apply(int node,int length,long delta) { sums[node] += delta * length; pending[node] += delta; }
    private void push(int node,int left,int right) {
        int middle = left + (right-left)/2;
        apply(node*2,middle-left,pending[node]); apply(node*2+1,right-middle,pending[node]); pending[node]=0;
    }
    private void bounds(int left,int right) {
        if (left<0 || right>count || left>=right) throw new IllegalArgumentException("range");
    }
    void add(int left,int right,long delta) { bounds(left,right); add(1,0,count,left,right,delta); }
    private void add(int node,int left,int right,int from,int until,long delta) {
        if (until<=left || right<=from) return;
        if (from<=left && right<=until) { apply(node,right-left,delta); return; }
        push(node,left,right); int middle=left+(right-left)/2;
        add(node*2,left,middle,from,until,delta); add(node*2+1,middle,right,from,until,delta);
        sums[node]=sums[node*2]+sums[node*2+1];
    }
    long sum(int left,int right) { bounds(left,right); return sum(1,0,count,left,right); }
    private long sum(int node,int left,int right,int from,int until) {
        if (until<=left || right<=from) return 0;
        if (from<=left && right<=until) return sums[node];
        push(node,left,right); int middle=left+(right-left)/2;
        return sum(node*2,left,middle,from,until)+sum(node*2+1,middle,right,from,until);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        CapacityRangeTree ledger=new CapacityRangeTree(new long[]{10,20,30,40});
        ledger.add(1,4,5); System.out.println(ledger.sum(0,4));
        ledger.add(0,2,-3); System.out.println(ledger.sum(1,3));
        try { ledger.sum(2,2); } catch (IllegalArgumentException rejected) { System.out.println("empty range rejected"); }
    }
}

Output

115
57
empty range rejected

Costs and boundaries

Construction costs O(n) time and O(n) storage. Each interval addition or sum query takes O(log n) time with O(log n) recursion depth. The bound is for one contiguous interval; arbitrary disjoint batches add more operations. This implementation is not persistent or thread-safe.

Common Mistakes

  • Push pending work before descending into part of an interval.
  • Use one interval convention consistently.
  • Do not assume long arithmetic cannot overflow.
